# Intake Brief: Allow cards to be discarded from the hand

## Problem statement

Main Street's engine already supports discarding a card from the player's hand, but the player cannot invoke it (there is no UI affordance) and the existing rule makes it **free**, whereas the requested design charges a **reputation cost equal to the card's coin cost**. This item adds the player-facing discard control and replaces the free rule with the reputation penalty.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they need to free hand capacity by discarding an unwanted card, and they should feel the trade-off of paying reputation for it.
- **TCE developers** — maintainers of Main Street's AI, Monte Carlo harness, tutorial, save-load, and docs, all of which reference discard-from-hand and must stay consistent.

Example user stories:

- "As a player, I want to discard a card I no longer need from my hand so I can make room for a better one."
- "As a player, I want discarding to cost reputation equal to the card's coin cost, so discarding is a meaningful decision rather than free."
- "As a player, I want the discard control in the End Turn slot so I can find it without hunting."
- "As a player, I never want a discard to push my reputation below zero."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **UI affordance and trigger:** Once a hand card is selected, a **[Discard]** button is rendered in the action bar's rightmost slot — the position occupied by **[End Turn]** in the market phase (the same slot `placing-from-hand` currently gives **[Cancel]**). Clicking it discards the selected hand card and returns the UI to the market phase; **[Cancel]** remains available alongside it (shifted left). No confirmation dialog is shown (producer decision). The button is created via `createActionButton`, positioned via the existing SLL layout values, and labelled with the reputation cost it will deduct.
- **Reputation penalty:** `discardFromHand` deducts `card.cost` from `state.resourceBank.reputation`, **clamped at 0** (reputation is never negative). The penalty applies to **every family** (business, community-space, upgrade, event) and uses each card's listed coin `cost`; 0-cost cards cost nothing. The discard is **not** gated on affordability (a low-reputation player may still discard, down to 0).
- **Action-free and reversible:** Discarding consumes **no daily action** (`state.actionsRemaining` is unchanged), preserving the current action economy. Undo/redo via `discardFromHandCommand` restores the hand, the family discard pile, and the reputation deducted.
- **AI accounting:** The AI no longer treats discard as free: its discard enumeration/evaluation weighs the reputation cost (e.g. only discards when the capacity benefit outweighs the reputation loss, preferring lower-cost cards). Monte Carlo baselines are re-run and re-baselined where the change moves the design-intent bands.
- **Documentation:** The rules docs, the Main Street README, and the in-game HUD tooltip that currently describe discard as free are updated to state the reputation cost; the engine/schema doc comments ("for free") are corrected. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Quality gates:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- Button placement is fixed by the producer: the End Turn slot (rightmost action-bar position).
- Reputation floor is fixed by the producer: allow the discard and clamp at 0; do **not** block on affordability.
- No confirmation dialog.
- Applies to all card families.
- Discarding stays action-free.
- Do not implement the action-economy item (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R); only preserve its "discard is free of actions" stance.
- New UI must follow the SLL requirement and reuse `createActionButton`; feedback must follow AGENTS rule 8 (animation + SFX via `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS.DISCARD`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- **Engine:** `discardFromHand(state, handIndex)` (`example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketHand.ts:149`) removes the card and routes it to the matching family discard pile. Its doc comment explicitly says "for free"; it deducts nothing.
- **Wiring:** `DiscardFromHandAction` (`MainStreetEngineTypes.ts:80`), `executeAction` (`MainStreetEngineActions.ts:242`), undo command `discardFromHandCommand` (`MainStreetCommands.ts:436`), hint text (`MainStreetHint.ts:182`), and AI enumeration (`MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:578`, `:1631` — only when the hand is full).
- **No human UI:** no button, right-click, drag target, or shortcut triggers a discard in `example-games/main-street/scenes/`. The HUD tooltip advertises "Free: re-roll market, sell, discard, end turn" (`MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:106`) and the rules doc lists "Discarding from hand" under free operations (`docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:281`).
- **Action bar:** `refreshActionButtons` (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts:262`) draws the market phase's **[End Turn]** at `rightX - btnW` and the `placing-from-hand` phase's **[Cancel]** at the same slot.
- **Selection:** `scene.pendingHandIndex` + `scene.uiPhase` (`'market' | 'placing-from-hand' | 'animating' | ...`). Business/community-space and upgrade hand clicks enter `placing-from-hand`; event hand clicks auto-play via `onPlayHeldEvent`.
- **Reputation:** `state.resourceBank.reputation`; the salary deduction clamps at 0 (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1185`), providing the clamp precedent.
- **Discard pile state:** `state.discards.{business,communitySpace,upgrade,event}`.

## Desired change

- Render a **[Discard]** button in the End Turn slot when a hand card is selected (during `placing-from-hand`, alongside [Cancel]), and wire it to a new undoable scene handler (`onDiscardHandCard`) that executes `discardFromHandCommand`, plays the discard SFX/animation, logs the action, and refreshes.
- Make the selected hand card discardable for **all** families (see Assumption A for the event-card selection approach).
- Change `discardFromHand` to deduct the card's `cost` from reputation, clamped at 0; update its doc comment and the action-type comment.
- Update the AI evaluation, hint text, HUD tooltip, rules docs, README, and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` — `discardFromHand` deducts reputation = `card.cost` (clamped at 0); update the "for free" doc comment.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — update the `DiscardFromHandAction` doc comment (no longer "for free").
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — verify `discardFromHandCommand` snapshot/undo covers the reputation change (no action-cost change).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render the [Discard] button in the End Turn slot when a hand card is selected; show the reputation cost on the button/label.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — new `onDiscardHandCard` handler; selection handling across families.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — selected-hand-card state (or reuse `pendingHandIndex`) and method delegation.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` / `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — hand-card click wiring so every family can be selected for discard.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — weigh the reputation cost in discard enumeration/evaluation.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHint.ts` — update the discard hint text.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — remove/adjust the "Free: … discard" wording.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — move discard out of the free-operations list and document the reputation cost and clamp.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — document the discard reputation cost.
- `tests/main-street/discard-from-hand.test.ts` (new) and updates to `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/command-action-economy.test.ts` — cover rep deduction, clamp at 0, all families, action-free, undo, and the UI trigger.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2** (completed) — "Expand player hand to 3 slots and rework marketplace to single row". It established the current rule: "discarding from hand is free, allowed any time during the player's turn, and sends the card to its corresponding discard pile." This item **reverses** the free rule, so its docs/tests must be updated in lockstep.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (open) — "Limit player actions to one action per turn (action economy)". Its intake lists discard among free operations; the reputation cost must not be mistaken for an action cost. Not implemented here.
- **CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7** (completed) — "Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street" (hand/discard economy precedent).
- **CG-0MQQHCK2I006KJY5** (completed) — "Move hand centering logic into hand component" (HandView/selection precedent).
- **CG-0MRH2FERF001OGWB** (completed) — "Extract CardMemoryTracker into generic core AI memory system" (AI evaluation precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A — event-card selection (UI):** the [Discard] button acts on the *selected* hand card. Business/community-space and upgrade cards already enter `placing-from-hand` on click (`pendingHandIndex`), which supplies the selection. Event cards auto-play on click (`onPlayHeldEvent`), so to make them discardable without silently dropping the click-to-play behaviour, the implementation should introduce a selection step for events (click selects + highlights; the action bar offers **[Play]** alongside **[Discard]**). If planning finds this regresses tutorial step T14 ("Triggering Events") or its E2E parts, the UI selection for events should be handled behind a small follow-up item while the engine penalty (AC2) still covers all families. To be confirmed during planning.
- **Assumption B — clamp semantics:** reputation is deducted but never below 0; the discard is always permitted regardless of current reputation (producer decision).
- **AI/Monte Carlo drift:** making discard costly changes AI behaviour and may move Monte Carlo scores; re-baseline only with justification, never silently widen the bands.
- **Tutorial gating:** the discard handler must respect `isTutorialActionAllowed` so a discard cannot bypass a required tutorial step.
- **Scope-creep risk:** alternate discard triggers (right-click, drag-to-discard), confirmation dialogs, and affordability gating were explicitly declined by the producer — record as linked work, do not implement.
- **Docs/consistency risk:** the "free operations" wording appears in the rules doc, README, and HUD tooltip; leaving any of them stale will mislead players.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (player trigger):** "There is currently no way for the human player to discard from hand. How should a discard be initiated?" — **Answer (operator, interactive):** "(b) select a hand card, then click a dedicated [Discard] button, placed where the End Turn button goes." Research: `MainStreetRendererHud.ts:262` renders [End Turn] at the rightmost action-bar slot; `placing-from-hand` reuses that slot for [Cancel]. Accepted: [Discard] occupies the End Turn slot.
- **Q2 (reputation floor / affordability):** "If the reputation penalty would drop reputation below 0 (or the player has less reputation than the card's cost), what should happen?" — **Answer (operator, interactive):** "(b) allow it and clamp reputation at 0." Research: salary deduction clamps at 0 (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1185`). Accepted: always allow; `Math.max(0, reputation - cost)`.
- **Q3 (scope confirmation):** "Does discarding remain action-free? Does the penalty apply to all families? Should there be a confirmation dialog? Should the AI weigh the reputation cost?" — **Answer (operator, interactive):** "action-free, all-families, no confirmation, yes weigh reputation cost." Accepted as stated. Research: current `discardFromHand` is free and family-routed; AI enumerates discard only when the hand is full (`MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:578`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7** – Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCK2I006KJY5** – Move hand centering logic into hand component (completed)
- **CG-0MRH2FERF001OGWB** – Extract CardMemoryTracker into generic core AI memory system (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: allow, card, cards, cost, discard, hand, reduce, reputation, should
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: allow, card, cards, cost, discard, hand, reduce, reputation, should
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: allow, card, cards, cost, discard, discarded, hand, reduce, reputation

# Tax Audit should collect 45% of banked coins

## Problem statement

The Main Street Tax Audit incident currently charges a flat 300-coin penalty
(`card-data.csv` row `evt-tax`, `coinDelta = -300`). A flat fee is regressive:
it is trivial for a late-game player with thousands of banked coins and
crippling for an early-game player with a few hundred. The Tax Audit should
instead scale with the player's wealth — collecting **45% of banked coins** —
so the consequence stays meaningful at every stage. Employing the **Accountant**
staff card should soften the blow, reducing the rate to **25%**.

## Users

- **Players** — Want incidents that scale with their economic position so a
  tax audit remains a real setback late-game and is survivable early-game.
- **Players who hire the Accountant** — Want that hiring decision to have a
  tangible, thematic payoff (tax mitigation) in addition to its existing
  market-refresh discount.
- **AI / Monte Carlo balance harness** — Needs the projected cost of the Tax
  Audit (and its Accept/Reject chain evaluation) to reflect the percentage
  mechanic, so simulations stay accurate.
- **TCE developers / producers** — Need a data-driven, testable mechanic that
  extends the existing `EventCard` model without breaking flat-delta events.

### User stories

- "As a player, I want a Tax Audit to take a proportional share of my banked
  coins, so the penalty is fair whether I am rich or poor."
- "As a player, I want hiring the Accountant to reduce my Tax Audit rate from
  45% to 25%, so the staff card feels worth its cost."
- "As an AI player, I want the projected cost of a Tax Audit to use the same
  percentage math as the live game, so my accept/reject decisions are correct."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Percentage collection** — When the Tax Audit (`evt-tax`) incident resolves
   on the Accept path, the coin loss equals **45% of the player's banked coins
   at resolution time** (`state.resourceBank.coins` before the effect).
   *Verification:* unit test seeds a known coin balance, forces `evt-tax`,
   accepts, and asserts the exact resulting balance.
2. **Accountant mitigation** — When the player has the Accountant staff card,
   the Tax Audit rate is **25%** instead of 45%. *Verification:* unit test with
   the Accountant employed asserts a 25% balance delta.
3. **No negative balance** — The coin loss is clamped so `resourceBank.coins`
   never drops below 0 (a tax audit cannot bankrupt a player into negative
   coins). *Verification:* unit test with a low balance asserts the floor at 0.
4. **Pre-existing flat-delta events unchanged** — All other events (including
   the rest of the Tax Escalation chain: `evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)
   continue to apply their flat `coinDelta` values exactly as before.
   *Verification:* regression test asserting an unchanged flat event's delta.
5. **AI projection parity** — `projectEventCoinDelta()` (used for AI
   affordability/accept-reject decisions) returns the same percentage-based
   magnitude for the Tax Audit as the live resolution path.
   *Verification:* unit test asserting projection equals the applied delta.
6. **Tests** — Unit tests cover percentage resolution, Accountant mitigation,
   zero-balance clamping, flat-event regression, and AI-projection parity.
   *Verification:* targeted `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/`.
7. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
8. **Full suite** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven** — The 45% / 25% rates must be defined as named constants
  (not magic literals scattered through the engine) and referenced from the
  card data or a single config site.
- **Backward compatible** — Existing saves and cards without the new
  percentage field must load and behave exactly as before. The new fields must
  be optional.
- **Deterministic** — The percentage calculation must not consume RNG (it is
  derived from the coin balance), preserving replay/transcript determinism.
- **Chain semantics preserved** — The Accept/Reject dual-choice behaviour of
  the Tax Escalation chain (CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128) is unchanged; only the
  magnitude of the Accept effect changes.
- **Formatting** — The activity-log line for the Tax Audit must show the
  actual coins lost (e.g. "Tax Audit (-225 coins)"), consistent with existing
  `describeEventEffects` output.

## Existing state

- **Tax Audit card**: `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` line 42 —
  `event,evt-tax,Tax Audit,...,All,,-300,0,...,true,,evt-tax-inquiry,,` — flat
  `coinDelta = -300`, `hasChoices = true`, `acceptNextCardId = null`,
  `rejectNextCardId = evt-tax-inquiry`.
- **EventCard model**: `MainStreetCards.ts:385` — `coinDelta: number` and
  `reputationDelta: number` only; no percentage field. `hasChoices`,
  `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` added by CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
- **Event resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEvent()` (~line 546)
  applies `state.resourceBank.coins += applyReputationMultiplier(cDelta(event.coinDelta), ...)`
  for `target: 'All'`; staff incident mitigation (`computeIncidentSkillBuffs`)
  already reduces negative incident coin deltas by a percentage.
- **Choice resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEventChoice()` (~line 2088)
  calls `resolveEvent()` on Accept and skips it on Reject.
- **AI projection**: `MainStreetEngine.ts:2212` `projectEventCoinDelta()` and
  `eventSeverity()` (~2237) read `event.coinDelta` directly.
- **Accountant card**: `card-data.csv` line 141 — `staff-accountant` with
  `refreshCostDiscount` only (`StaffCard.refreshCostDiscount`,
  `MainStreetCards.ts:557`). "Adds +1 hand slot and makes investment refreshes
  cost 1 less."
- **Difficulty config**: `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` has incident draw pacing
  parameters but no per-event percentage rates.

## Desired change

1. **Card data** — Add an optional percentage field to the event card model
   (e.g. `coinPercentDelta?: number`, value `-0.45` for Tax Audit) and set it
   on `evt-tax` in `card-data.csv` (new column). Update the CSV header and the
   `EventCard` interface/serialisation in `MainStreetCards.ts`.
2. **Engine resolution** — In `resolveEvent()`, when an event carries a
   percentage delta, compute the coin loss from the pre-effect
   `resourceBank.coins`, clamp at 0, and log the actual amount. Flat-delta
   events take the existing path.
3. **Accountant mitigation** — Add a staff-level tax-rate override (e.g.
   `taxAuditRate?: number` / `taxPctDiscount?: number` on `StaffCard`, aggregated
   across `state.staffCards`) so an employed Accountant sets the Tax Audit rate
   to 25%. The engine applies it when resolving the percentage event.
4. **AI projection** — Update `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` to
   mirror the percentage math for percentage events.
5. **Tests** — New unit tests for the five verification points in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Add percentage field/column; set
  Tax Audit to 45%; add Accountant tax-rate field if card-level.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Extend `EventCard` with
  `coinPercentDelta?`; extend `StaffCard` with the tax-rate field; parse from CSV.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveEvent()` percentage
  branch + clamping; `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` parity;
  Accountant-rate lookup.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — (only if a typed config field
  is needed for defaults; otherwise untouched).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — Likely home for a
  `computeTaxAuditRate(staffCards)` helper, consistent with existing staff-buff
  helpers.
- `tests/main-street/` — New/updated unit tests (percentage resolution,
  Accountant mitigation, clamping, flat-event regression, AI parity).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — rounding mode is `Math.round`** (standard). The engine already
  uses an integer-rounding helper for fractional effects; the same convention
  is assumed. **OPEN QUESTION Q1** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — no minimum beyond the 0 floor**: the tax can round to 0 for a
  player with very few coins; there is no "always at least 1" rule.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q2** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — scope is Tax Audit only**: the percentage mechanic applies to
  `evt-tax` only; `evt-tax-error` (-200) and `evt-tax-inquiry` (-600) keep
  their flat values (AC4). **OPEN QUESTION Q3** — producer to confirm whether
  the whole Tax Escalation chain should convert.
- **Assumption — Accountant mechanism is a card-level numeric field** (Option A,
  mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`) rather than a new specialization skill.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q4** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — rates are difficulty-independent**: 45% / 25% are fixed for
  Easy/Medium/Hard. **OPEN QUESTION Q5** — producer to confirm.
- **Risk — ordering vs `applyReputationMultiplier`**: the percentage must be
  computed from the pre-effect balance, then the reputation multiplier applied
  in the same order as existing deltas. Mitigation: a focused test with
  non-default reputation.
- **Risk — AI/Renderer divergence**: the Tax Audit magnitude appears in the
  engine, the AI projection, and possibly the renderer/animator. Mitigation:
  route all three through one shared helper.
- **Risk — scope creep**: converting the full Tax Escalation chain (and other
  events) is a natural follow-on; recorded as a separate work item if the
  producer wants it, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128** — Story-driven event chains with dual-choice
  consequences (completed) — defines the Tax Escalation chain and the
  Accept/Reject path that this item's effect feeds into.
- **CG-0MM8RAXJ61L6BG8Z** — Rework event system: reclassify triggers, incident
  queue, investments row, player hand UI (completed) — Tax Audit classified as
  an Incident.
- **CG-0MM8RCFZU03GY009** — Reclassify event triggers and rename Rainy Night
  (completed).
- **CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58** — Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting (open) —
  the Tax Escalation chain source.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** — Accountant refresh-discount ability (Group F) —
  the existing Accountant staff buff this change builds alongside.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 — Rounding:** When 45% (or 25%) of banked coins produces a fractional
  result, which rounding mode should be used?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used to draft: `Math.round()` (standard), matching the engine's
    existing integer-rounding convention. Recorded on the work item for
    producer confirmation.
- **Q2 — Minimum/Maximum bounds:** Should the tax be floored at 0, floored at
  1 coin, or capped at the total balance?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: clamp the loss so coins never go below 0 (no negative
    balance); no "at least 1" floor.
- **Q3 — Chain cards:** Apply the percentage to Tax Audit only, or to all three
  Tax Escalation cards (`evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: Tax Audit only (per the work-item title); the other two
    keep flat values.
- **Q4 — Accountant mechanism:** How should the 45%→25% reduction be
  represented — a card-level numeric field, a specialization skill, or
  another mechanism?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: card-level numeric field on `StaffCard` (Option A),
    mirroring the existing `refreshCostDiscount` pattern.
- **Q5 — Difficulty scaling:** Are 45% / 25% fixed across Easy/Medium/Hard, or
  difficulty-scaled?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: fixed across all difficulties.
- **Q6 — Research:** Inspected `card-data.csv` (Tax Audit `evt-tax` row; Tax
  Escalation rows `evt-tax-error`/`evt-tax-inquiry`; `staff-accountant` row),
  `MainStreetCards.ts` (`EventCard`, `StaffCard`, `refreshCostDiscount`),
  `MainStreetEngine.ts` (`resolveEvent`, `resolveEventChoice`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`), `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`,
  `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`, and related work item CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
  Confirmed: banked coins = `state.resourceBank.coins`; Tax Audit is a
  `target: 'All'` Incident with an Accept/Reject chain; no existing
  percentage-of-balance event effect exists.

## Problem

The Reputation line in the score tooltip displays an awkward `×` symbol before the colon separator (e.g. `Reputation ×: 5`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Remove the `×` from the Reputation label in the score tooltip so it reads `Reputation: 5` instead of `Reputation ×: 5`.
2. All related documentation and i18n keys are updated consistently.
3. Full project test suite must pass with the change.

## Constraints

- The `×` symbol is used correctly elsewhere in the tooltip (e.g. showing multipliers like `×1.038`) — only remove it from the Reputation label.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` line 95: `scoreBreakdownReputation: 'Reputation ×'`
- Line 303 builds the output: `${t(HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS.scoreBreakdownReputation)}: ${repContribution}` → renders as `Reputation ×: 5`

## Desired change

- Change `'Reputation ×'` to `'Reputation'` on line 95 of `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — Default English string templates

# Activity log shows coins, reputation and score

The last entry in the activity log should show the end-of-turn totals for **coins**, **reputation**, and **score** on a single line, alongside the existing per-turn net summary row (which shows the turn's deltas).

## Problem Statement

The activity log already displays a per-turn net summary row (`Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep (score: +/−Z)`), added in CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA and extended with the score delta in the first pass of this item. The net row shows *deltas* only. The player also wants to see their **running totals** for coins, reputation, and score at a glance at the end of each turn — without having to look at the HUD.

## Users and User Stories

- **Player:** "After I click End Turn, I want to see my total coins, reputation, and score at a glance in the activity log — not have to look at the HUD."
- **Player:** "I want to see how much my score changed this turn, so I can tell whether my actions were productive."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The activity log's end-of-turn net summary row is extended to include the score delta. Format: `Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep (score: +/−Z)` — coins, rep, and score deltas all on a single line.
- **AC2:** The score delta is computed as the difference between the current `finalScore` (after EndCheck) and the `finalScore` from the previous turn's end. If the score is unchanged, the entry shows `(score: +0)` or `(score: 0)`.
- **AC3:** The score delta entry appears alongside the existing net row — i.e. the existing `appendTurnNetRow()` function is extended, not replaced.
- **AC4:** The score snapshot survives save/load and replay (carried in `MainStreetState` clone/restore/serialization alongside the existing `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep` fields).
- **AC5:** Tests: unit tests for the extended net-row format pass; full unit suite green.
- **AC6 (audit follow-up, 2026-09-16):** A further activity-log entry immediately after the net row shows the **running totals** for coins, reputation, and score on a **new line**. Format: `Turn N totals: X coins, Y rep, Z score`. The totals line is the final log entry for a completed turn (including premature-exit and competitive closing paths).

## Constraints

- Main Street only — no generalisation to other example games at this time.
- Deltas stay on the existing net row; the totals go on a new, separate line.
- Score delta, not running total, on the delta line.

## Existing State

- `appendTurnNetRow(state, turnEnded)` now lives in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` (the engine was decomposed after the first pass) and appends the net row using `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep`/`dayStartScore` snapshots.
- `finalScore` is updated each EndCheck via `updateScore()` which calls `computeScore()`.
- `dayStartCoins`, `dayStartRep`, and `dayStartScore` are stored on `MainStreetState` and survive clone/restore/serialization.
- Related completed work: CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA (Per-turn net coin/rep summary row).

## Desired Change

Extend `appendTurnNetRow()` to also append a running-totals line after the delta row:

1. Keep the existing net row (`Turn N net: +X coins, +Y rep (score: +/−Z)`).
2. Append a totals line: `Turn N totals: X coins, Y rep, Z score`.
3. Ensure the totals line is the final entry and does not disturb existing ordering guarantees (game-over banner still precedes the net row).
4. Update tests to assert both lines and the total-vs-delta distinction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `appendTurnNetRow()`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineDayStart.ts` — `executeDayStart()` (snapshot)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `dayStartScore` wiring
- `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` — net-row + totals tests
- `tests/main-street/turn-cash-net.test.ts` — log-ordering tests
- `tests/main-street/turn-cash-repro.test.ts` — decomposition test

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTGX46HX005FQPA** (Per-turn net coin/rep summary row in activity log) — sibling child of CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ; adds coins+rep net row
- **CG-0MTGX3XSH005VRUI** (All resource-mutating log entries gain effective deltas) — sibling child of CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ; enriches individual action entries with effective deltas
- **CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79** (Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI) — original log implementation

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the score appear on the same line as the existing net row, or as a separate line?" — Answer: Same line for the *delta*; the **totals** go on a new line (audit follow-up, 2026-09-16).
- Q: "Should the log show the running total score, or the score delta from the previous turn?" — Answer: Both — delta on the net row, running total on the totals line.
- Q: "Does this apply to all example games, or Main Street only?" — Answer: Main Street only.

# Feature: Config-driven game discovery (F3)

## Goal

Replace static imports in `main.ts` with a Vite plugin that reads a selected `configs/<preset>.json` and generates the game registry from sibling game dirs. Define the `GAME_INFO` convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `GAME_INFO` convention documented and followed: each game exports `GAME_INFO: GameEntry` alongside its scene (`<GameName>Scene.ts`) — shape `{ sceneKey, title, description, thumbnail }`. Thumbnails are per-game assets.
2. Vite plugin (e.g. `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) reads `configs/<preset>.json` selected via `GAMES_CONFIG` env / CLI flag and generates a virtual or file-based game-registry module consumed by `main.ts`. Config entry shape: `{ id, path, scenePath }` with sibling paths `../tce-<game>`.
3. `main.ts` no longer has hardcoded game imports — the game registry is fully derived from the selected config. Gym (in core) remains always present.
4. Core-only build (config with no games or no config) shows empty/placeholder selector state; partial and full configs show exactly the listed games.

- Straight to B: read-only `configs/*.json` presets (no ephemeral A/C CLI-filter phase that would be replaced).

# Synergy bonus coins animate along synergy lines to receiving card coin matrix

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature**

## Problem statement

End-turn synergy bonuses are folded into each slot's base income (`currentIncome` / `baseIncome`) so the phased `synergy` income phase never shows coins, and the synergy lines are only a static indicator. Players cannot see *where* synergy income came from — which neighbor gave which bonus and how it lands on the receiving card's coin grid.

## Users

- **Player** — "When my turn ends I want to see synergy coins travel along the glowing synergy lines from the giving card's edge to the receiving card, slowly enough to follow, then land in the receiving card's coin matrix — so the synergy economy reads as a spatial transfer, not a hidden number."
- **Player (reduced motion / replay)** — "I still want the synergy phase to pace and label clearly, but without the line flights; replay/headless should show nothing."

### User stories

- As a player with two adjacent synergistic businesses, when the income phases run I see coins leave the edge of one card, slide along the synergy line at a readable speed, arrive at the edge of the other card and count into its coin grid — in both directions for each pair.
- As a player with a business that has two synergistic neighbors, I see a separate stream along each synergy line into that card's grid, with the sum matching the card's credited synergy bonus.
- As a player with reduced motion enabled, the synergy phase still labels and paces but does not animate line flights; the grid still reflects the credited total at collect.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Phase data separates synergy from base** — `SlotPhaseBreakdown` (and the `applyIncome`/`computeIncome` producers) expose board adjacency synergy as a non-zero `synergyBonus` per slot when applicable, and `baseIncome` no longer includes synergy. The per-slot sum `baseIncome + synergyBonus + repBonus + eventDeltas + upcomingDeltas` still equals the credited total; existing `SlotIncome.total` / transcript totals are unchanged. Covered by unit tests (single pair, multi-neighbor, extended-range `synergyRangeBonus`, zero-synergy, sold-slot, same-type penalty).
2. **Bidirectional line-to-grid coin flights (600 ms)** — During the `synergy` income phase, for every synergy pair (`computeSynergyPairs` / `synergyLineEndpoints` clipped `p1`→`p2` geometry — the shared slot-rect-clipped line), coins animate **in both directions** along the line: from the giver's edge (`p1`) to the receiver's edge (`p2`) and vice-versa, each over **~600 ms** (`INCOME_FLIGHT_MS`) with ~60 ms stagger. Each direction carries the receiver's synergy amount attributable to that neighbor (icons via `iconsForAmount` / `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, clamp ≥1 when amount >0). Arrival increments the receiver's on-card `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid` (incremental `displayed` accumulation, same as base/reputation phases) so grids stay visible until the final collect.
3. **Phased choreography integration** — The synergy phase no longer short-circuits when bonuses exist; it runs between `base` and `reputation` on the existing phase schedule (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS=2200 ms`, phase label "Synergy"), reuses the shared `synergyLineEndpoints` helper (so animated lines never drift from static lines), and preserves the final grid→HUD collection, `incomeCollectionActive` suppression, per-coin `COIN_POP` SFX via `moveGameObject`/`soundManager`, and stagger/overlap handling for multiple pairs (including diagnonal and extended-range pairs).
4. **Accessibility & presentation-only guarantees** — Reduced motion keeps the synergy phase label + pacing but suppresses line flights (no `moveGameObject` tweens), matching other phases; replay/headless (`scene.replayMode`) performs no rendering or audio. The feature is presentation-only: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow, is non-blocking, and failures are swallowed so the turn always advances.
5. **Tests + docs** — New/extended unit tests for phase-data separation and per-neighbor attribution; browser tests for bidirectional `p1→p2` flights (assert start near giver edge, end near receiver grid / no (0,0) regression), multi-neighbor, extended-range, and reduced-motion/replay paths; existing income/coin-grid suites remain green. Docs updated (`docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` or equivalent, inline code comments, scene README/help text as needed).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates state/transcript/turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8); non-blocking, failures swallowed; runs inside the turn-advance window like the existing `animateIncomePhases`.
- Reuse existing helpers: `synergyLineEndpoints` (clipped slot-rect geometry), `CoinGrid`/`createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`packCoins`, `moveGameObject` + `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention, `COIN_POP`), `computeSynergyPairs`, `COINS_PER_ICON` scaling.
- Respect reduced-motion (`SettingsStore` / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption; mute/volume honored via `soundManager`.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop`.
- Must not regress CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ (phased income), CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation), or the `currentIncome`/`currentReputationPerTurn` caching contract.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAdjacency.computeSynergyBonus` / `computeBusinessIncome` use a percentage formula (`effectiveBase * synergyCoinBonus * bonusPerNeighbor * N`) with same-type 0.6 penalty and `synergyRangeBonus` 8-way Chebyshev range; `computeSynergyPairs` enumerates pairs via 8-way `neighbors()`.
- `applyIncome` / `applyCompetitiveIncome` and `computeIncome` fold board adjacency synergy into `card.currentIncome` → `SlotIncome.baseIncome` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown.baseIncome`; `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` is always `0` (hand synergy removed CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN). `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` therefore short-circuits the `synergy` case (`iconsForAmount(roundHalf(synergyBonus)) === 0`).
- `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` is the single source of truth for clipped `p1`→`p2` + `mid` geometry, shared by `MainStreetRenderer.drawSynergyLines()` and `MainStreetAnimator.animateSynergyFormation()`.
- `MainStreetAnimator` phased choreography (`base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`, `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS=2200`, `INCOME_FLIGHT_MS=600`, `INCOME_FLIGHT_STAGGER_MS=60`) creates a `CoinGrid` per producing slot parented to the card container; `countOutCoins`/`flyCoinsIn`/`flyCoinsOut` incrementally `revealInGrid`; `collectIncomeGrids` flies grids to HUD (`coinX = gameW*0.25+70`).
- `coin-grid.ts`: integer economy, `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `packCoins`/`gridColumns` 5→10→15 with shrink/overlap, `createCoinGrid` anchored to card container.

## Desired change

1. **Separate synergy in phase data** — Teach `computeIncome` and `applyIncome` (and competitive variant) to populate `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` from `computeSynergyBonus` (or an equivalent per-slot derivation that stays consistent with `currentIncome` + same-type/staff/upgrade semantics) and reduce `baseIncome` by that amount so the sum is preserved. Decide and document whether `SlotIncome` (preview path) also separates or stays total-preserving for backward compat; the animation consumes `SlotPhaseBreakdown`.
2. **Animate synergy lines as coin conduits** — Replace the synergy phase's midpoint `flyCoinsIn` with a bidirectional line traversal: for each `SynergyPair`, derive the clipped segment `p1` (giver edge) → `p2` (receiver edge) via `synergyLineEndpoints(pair, layout)` for both directions; spawn `iconsForAmount(per-neighbor synergy share)` coin visuals at `p1`, tween each along the segment to `p2` (600 ms, `Quad.easeIn`, 60 ms stagger), then on arrival `revealInGrid` on the receiver's `IncomePhaseSlot` handle (edge→grid is the tween landing → grid pop; no extra teleport needed beyond detaching the flight visual). Per-neighbor share is `effectiveBase * rate * bonusPerNeighbor` (uniform across neighbors) or the proportional split of the slot's `synergyBonus` across its `N` matching neighbors — choose the one that sums to `synergyBonus` and document it.
3. **Keep all other phases/behaviors intact** — phase ordering/labels/timing, `incomeCollectionActive`, SFX, reduced-motion/replay gates, and grid-to-HUD collection remain as today.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — separate per-slot board synergy from base in `computeIncome`/`applyIncome`/`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus`; keep `SlotPhaseBreakdown`/`IncomeResult` contract consistent.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — rework `runIncomePhase('synergy')` + `synergyPhaseSources()` to bidirectional `p1→p2` flights via `synergyLineEndpoints`; add helper to attribute per-neighbor coin counts and to land into `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/synergyLineEndpoints.ts` — shared clipped geometry (no change expected, but its `p1`/`p2` are the flight endpoints).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — reference for static synergy line rendering; no change unless depth/z-ordering needs alignment.
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`iconsForAmount`/`COINS_PER_ICON` (no change expected).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn` wiring if phase data plumbing needs it (likely not).
- `tests/main-street/**` — new/updated unit + browser tests (phase data separation, bidirectional line flights, multi-neighbor, extended range, reduced motion).

## Related work

- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ "Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)" (completed) — phased choreography, `animateIncomePhases`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, `CoinGrid` accumulation, `INCOME_PHASE_*` timing.
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR "Synergy link formation animation" (completed) + CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B "synergyLineEndpoints" — shared clipped synergy geometry.
- CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN "Remove hand synergy — cards in hand must not affect street income" — synergy is board-only; `handSynergyTotal` stays 0.
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 "Integer economy (×100)" — `COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `Math.round`, `roundInt`.
- CG-0MRWGPR0G009Z5G6 / CG-0MRWLMNU9000ZFXC / CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4 "Percentage-based synergy formula" — `effectiveBase * rate * bonusPerNeighbor * N`.
- CG-0MSP1HCAS00785MP "8-way synergy adjacency + extended range" — `neighbors()` Chebyshev, `synergyRangeBonus`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Synergy attribution vs displayed total** — Splitting a slot's `synergyBonus` across `N` neighbors must sum exactly to the credited total (rounding with `roundInt`/`COINS_PER_ICON`). Mitigate: derive per-neighbor share from the same formula that produces `synergyBonus` and assert sum preservation in tests.
- **Line-to-grid handoff readability** — Flying along the line then popping into the grid must not look like the coin vanishes at the card edge. Mitigate: flight lands at the card edge (`p2`) then immediately triggers the grid pop (`revealInGrid`) with `COIN_POP` SFX.
- **Multi-pair staggering / visual clutter** — Multiple simultaneous line flights could overlap. Mitigate: per-line stagger (60 ms) and 600 ms duration; keep total synergy phase within the existing gap budget; no extra phase delay.
- **Geometry drift** — Animated lines must match static lines. Mitigate: consume `synergyLineEndpoints` directly; no duplicated math.
- **Scope creep** — This item is synergy phase only; no changes to reputation/event/upcoming phases, no new SFX keys, no deck redesign. Log extras as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (Map → user): "Direction per pair — both directions or single? If single, how is giver/receiver chosen?" — Answer (user): "yes both directions" — both `p1→p2` and `p2→p1` animate, one stream per card's bonus (i.e., each card in the pair receives coins along the line from its synergistic neighbor). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.
- Q2 (Map → user): "'Relatively slowly' + sequencing — how slow and sequential vs parallel per card with multiple neighbors?" — Answer (user): "lets try 600ms" — keep the existing flight duration (600 ms) as the line traversal speed; lines animate in parallel with stagger (60 ms). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.
- Q3 (Map → user): "Should the income data separate synergy from base, and should arriving coins count onto the coin matrix?" — Answer (user): "yes separate it out, yes arriving coins should count onto the coin grid" — `SlotPhaseBreakdown.synergyBonus` must be populated (board adjacency synergy no longer folded into `baseIncome`), and line arrivals must increment the receiving card's `CoinGrid` via `revealInGrid` accumulating until collect. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-10.

Research summary: Inspected `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (folded synergy in `currentIncome`/`baseIncome`, `computeSynergyBonus` percentage formula, `computeSynergyPairs` 8-way range), `MainStreetAnimator.ts` (phased `animateIncomePhases`/`runIncomePhase` synergy short-circuit, `synergyPhaseSources` midpoint sources, `createCoinGrid`/`revealInGrid`/`flyCoinsIn`/`collectIncomeGrids`, timing constants), `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` (clipped `p1`/`p2`/`mid` as single source of truth), and `coin-grid.ts` (`COINS_PER_ICON=100`, `packCoins` 5→10→15). Related work confirmed via `wl search` (synergy/income). Defaults for Q1–Q3 were posed and then confirmed by the user in this session.

## Mini-review record

- **1. Completeness:** Problem, users/stories, 5 measurable ACs + docs+suite ACs, constraints, existing/desired states, key files, related work, and Q&A appendix all present and actionable. No placeholders.
- **2. Capture fidelity:** User Q1–Q3 answers captured verbatim in the Appendix without invention; "relatively slowly" concretized as the requested 600 ms and "edge→edge then to coin matrix" as `p1→p2` via `synergyLineEndpoints` landing into `revealInGrid`.
- **3. Related-work & traceability:** Direct precedents linked (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR, CG-0MTRDX0DN004EECN, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6, percentage/8-way synergy items); shared helpers (`synergyLineEndpoints`, `CoinGrid`, `COINS_PER_ICON`) explicitly referenced; find-related report to be appended.
- **4. Risks & assumptions:** Added attribution/summing, handoff readability, staggering/clutter, geometry drift, and scope-creep guard with mitigations; assumptions (uniform per-neighbor share, 600 ms parallel stagger) documented.
- **5. Polish & handoff:** Tightened language, copy-pasteable file paths, measurable ACs with verification hooks (unit/browser/docs), and a 1–2 sentence headline in the finish summary.
## Related work (automated report)

# Intake Brief — Validate all card text (CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0)

## Problem statement

The integer-economy migration (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) scaled coin/reputation
**data** ×100 but only partially updated the **card text**. Business,
community-space, upgrade, and staff `description` fields were scaled, but every
event `effect` field was left at its pre-migration display-scale value (e.g.
`evt-festival` reads `+2 coins` while its `coinDelta` is `200`), and
`evt-shopping-spree` still shows a fractional `+2.5 coins` (data `250`).
Players therefore read card text that disagrees with the amount the engine
actually applies, with the activity log, and with the raw-integer HUD. The
same stale values also remain in every other player-visible surface that
repeats card coin/reputation amounts — card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy,
staff-skill descriptions, and the `docs/main-street/*` reference material.

## Users

- **Player** — needs each card's text to state the same coin/reputation amount
  that will actually be applied, so purchase/play decisions are informed.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs `card-data.csv` text and data columns to
  agree so balancing is based on accurate descriptions.
- **Developer / QA** — needs a durable check that catches future card-text/data
  drift instead of relying on manual review.

### User stories

- As a player, when I read an event card's effect text I see the same
  coin/reputation amount that the game applies and that the activity log shows.
- As a designer, I can trust that every card description matches its
  `card-data.csv` values without mental ×100 conversion.
- As a developer, a failing check tells me exactly which card's text no longer
  matches its data.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every player-visible card-text surface is ×100-consistent with card
   data.** Every numeric coin/reputation mention in card text equals the
   corresponding data column (`coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`,
   `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `reputationBonus`, `incomeBonus`,
   staff-skill magnitudes) under the documented ×100 scale. The audited
   surfaces are: the `card-data.csv` `description` and `effect` columns;
   card-face SVG text (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and committed SVG
   artifacts); tooltips (`MainStreetFormatting.ts`); tutorial copy
   (`TutorialFlow.ts`, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`); staff-skill descriptions
   (`MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`); and the `docs/main-street/*` reference
   material. All event `effect` texts are scaled (e.g. `evt-festival`
   `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`); `evt-shopping-spree` `+2.5 coins` →
   `+250 coins`. No fractional coin/reputation value remains in any
   player-visible card text.
2. **Non-coin/reputation numbers are unchanged.** Percentages (`45%`, `90%`,
   `120%`), durations (`3 turns`), hand-slot counts, levels, and the
   `{SYNERGY_RATE}` token are out of scope and verified unchanged.
3. **Automated regression test guards against drift.** An automated unit test
   parses every card's text coin/reputation mentions and asserts they match the
   card's data columns under the documented ×100 scale, failing with a message
   that identifies the offending card. The test must run in the `unit` profile
   and fail if a future edit desynchronises card text from card data.
4. **Tests and artifacts updated.** Existing test expectations that reference
   old text values are updated; committed card SVG artifacts are regenerated to
   match the corrected text; `npm run build` and the unit test profile pass.
5. **Documentation updated.** Every doc carrying stale fractional card values
   (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
   identified during implementation) is revised to the integer scale; code
   comments describing the old scale (e.g. the `{bonus}` example `+2 coins` in
   `TutorialFlow.ts`) are corrected. All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Text is corrected to match data; data
  values are not changed to match text.
- **Only coin/reputation amounts scale.** Percentage, rate, duration, and count
  values are untouched; `{SYNERGY_RATE}` stays a rate token resolved at render
  time.
- **Cover every player-visible surface (producer-confirmed).** Card-face SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs are all in scope,
  not just the CSV `description`/`effect` columns.
- **Automated tests required (producer-confirmed).** The regression guard is an
  automated unit test, not a manual checklist.
- **No rebalancing.** Apply text-only ×100 corrections; any balance change is a
  separate work item.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `card-data.csv` business/community-space/upgrade/staff `description` fields
  were scaled ×100 by CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6.
- Every event `effect` field retains its pre-migration value (small integers),
  while `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` were scaled ×100 — e.g. `evt-festival`
  `effect: "+2 coins to all Culture businesses and +1 reputation."`,
  `coinDelta: 200`, `reputationDelta: 100`.
- `evt-shopping-spree` is the only card with a fractional value in text:
  `"+2.5 coins to all Commerce businesses."` (`coinDelta: 250`).
- The HUD renders raw integers (`Coins: 1000`); the activity log renders raw
  integers via `describeEventEffects` (`+200 coins`); SpecificSynergy event
  tooltips show only the (small) `effect` text, so the mismatch is visible to
  players.
- `TutorialFlow.ts` resolves `{bonus}` from `coinDelta` (`+${coinDelta} coins`
  → `+200 coins`) but its doc comment still says `e.g. '+2 coins'`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (and several other `docs/main-street/*`
  files, including `specialization-skills.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, and `prd-multi-use-card-economy.md`)
  still use fractional values such as `+0.4/turn` and `0.25 coins/turn`.
- No automated test currently compares card text amounts against card data;
  existing card tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
  `card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
  `csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic fixtures.

## Desired change

Audit every player-visible card-text source — CSV text, card-face SVGs,
tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions, and docs — scale all
coin/reputation amounts to match the integer data (×100), remove the last
fractional value, add an automated regression test so text/data drift is caught
automatically, and refresh stale docs and comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — scale every event `effect` coin/rep
  amount ×100 and fix the `evt-shopping-spree` fractional value; check remaining
  `description` fields.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — tooltip rendering of
  `effect`/`description`; confirm text/data consistency.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face
  text; confirm integer rendering and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill
  descriptions; verify already-scaled values.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` doc comment and any
  tutorial card-value copy.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — tutorial copy referencing
  card coin/reputation values.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip coin/rep
  values and card detail lines.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — committed card-face SVG
  artifacts; regenerate after text corrections.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and the other `docs/main-street/*` files
  with stale fractions — update to the integer scale.
- `tests/main-street/**` — new automated card-text/data consistency test plus
  updated expectations.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — canonical card text/data source.
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — card catalogue with stale fractional values.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — card tooltip text builder.
  - `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — card-face SVG text.
  - `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — `{bonus}` interpolation and stale comment.
  - `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — staff-skill descriptions.
- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6)` —
    completed; the migration whose text updates this item validates.
  - `Dynamic synergy bonus text on business cards (difficulty-aware percentage, Option B) (CG-0MS9GS91E004OAF4)` —
    completed; dynamic card text rendering.
  - `Synergy bonus on business cards (CG-0MRXYHNHB006F0U9)` — completed;
    synergy text semantics.
  - `In main street log should show total effects (CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ)` —
    completed; log integer deltas that already disagree with event text.
  - `Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT)` —
    completed; tutorial copy review precedent.
  - `Fix card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting tests (CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH)` —
    completed; card rendering/formatting tests.
  - `Main Street Game over dialog is not showing text (CG-0MQ2IL40S0060FUG)` —
    completed; card/dialog text rendering precedent.
  - `Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7)` —
    completed; card-economy semantics behind the coin/rep values.
  - `Docs: tutorial-localization + README updates (CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU)` —
    completed; tutorial/doc text-update precedent.

> **Automated related-work report:** `/skill:find-related` was run and inserted
> a report into the work item. Its findings are folded into the list above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: event `effect` scaling direction (confirmed ×100).** Producer
  confirmed event effect text scales ×100 to match `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`,
  consistent with the already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer
  HUD/log. The regression test encodes this.
- **Risk: natural-language parsing fragility.** Comparing text amounts to data
  columns requires parsing prose. Mitigation: constrain the test to well-formed
  `[+-]?N coins?` / `[+-]?N reputation` patterns and/or an explicit per-card
  expected-value map, with a clear failure message naming the card.
- **Risk: scope creep into rebalancing.** Mitigation: apply only ×100 text
  corrections; file a separate balance work item for any value change.
- **Risk: missed text sources.** Coin/reputation copy lives in CSV text, SVGs,
  tooltips, tutorial strings, staff skills, and docs. Mitigation: grep the repo
  for fractional coin/rep patterns and for the `effect`/`description` columns,
  and regenerate committed SVG artifacts.
- **Risk: expanded scope increases effort.** Producer confirmed "cover
  everything" and automated tests, which widens the surface beyond the CSV and
  raises the estimate. Mitigation: effort/risk re-estimated after the scope
  confirmation.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** scope covers every player-visible surface that
  repeats card coin/reputation amounts (CSV text, SVGs, tooltips, tutorial
  copy, staff skills, docs); percentages, durations, and counts are out of
  scope.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** the regression guard is an automated unit test.
- **Assumption:** documentation updates cover the docs carrying stale card
  coin/reputation values; unrelated doc drift is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

An initial brief was drafted from the seed context, then three clarifying
questions were put to the producer and answered (2026-09-24, interactive
reply). The brief has been updated to the confirmed answers.

- **Q: Should event `effect` text be scaled ×100 to match
  `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (e.g. `+2 coins` → `+200 coins`)?** —
  **Answer (producer): yes.** Source: interactive reply; consistent with the
  already-scaled business descriptions and the raw-integer HUD/log. Research:
  `git show 192943c9` showed the migration scaled descriptions but not the
  event `effect` column; `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` and
  `MainStreetStateLog.ts` render raw integers.
- **Q: Is "all card text" limited to the `card-data.csv` `description`/`effect`
  columns, or should it cover tooltips/SVGs/tutorial copy/docs too?** —
  **Answer (producer): cover everything.** Source: interactive reply. The brief
  now scopes card-face SVGs, tooltips, tutorial copy, staff-skill descriptions,
  and `docs/main-street/*`.
- **Q: Is an automated regression test the expected way to "ensure" ongoing
  correctness, or is a one-time audit-and-fix sufficient?** —
  **Answer (producer): automated tests.** Source: interactive reply. AC3 is now
  a required automated unit test rather than a manual checklist.

**Research summary:** `wl show CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 --json` established the
migration contract (CSV ×100, integer-only UI). `git show 192943c9` confirmed
the migration scaled business/community/staff/upgrade descriptions but did not
touch the event `effect` column. A CSV parse of all 173 rows found exactly one
remaining fractional text value (`evt-shopping-spree`, `+2.5 coins` vs
`coinDelta=250`) and showed every event `effect` still at display scale
(e.g. `evt-festival` `+2 coins` vs `coinDelta=200`). `MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
`MainStreetStateLog.ts` (`describeEventEffects`), `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`,
`TutorialFlow.ts`, and `MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` were inspected to map the
text sources and confirm the HUD/log render raw integers. `docs/main-street/*`
was grepped and found to retain fractional values in `card-catalog.md` and
several other files. Existing tests (`event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`,
`card-currency-formatting.test.ts`, `card-schema-validation.test.ts`,
`csv-checksum.test.ts`) use synthetic data and contain no card-text/data
consistency guard. The producer's three answers (×100 direction, cover
everything, automated tests) were applied to the problem statement, AC1/AC3/AC5,
constraints, and risks.

# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
