# AGENTS.md exceeds context-budget threshold, blocking all pushes to dev (CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ)

**Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Problem statement

The pre-push context-budget gate rejects **every** push to `dev` because the committed `AGENTS.md` (46024 B) exceeds the committed `project_agents` threshold (45898 B) by 126 B. The breach is committed at `dev` HEAD (working tree clean), so it is not caused by any single in-flight change — it blocks all agents and developers until either `AGENTS.md` is trimmed or the threshold is refreshed. This is the **fifth** occurrence of the same drift class; the threshold has already been manually refreshed four times (`39555 → 41692 → 41706 → 43564 → 45898`).

## Users

- **Agent / developer pushing to `dev` (primary)** — Currently forced to bypass the gate with `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1` (undermining its value) or cannot push at all.
  - *Story:* As an agent completing a work item, I can push to `dev` without a `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1` bypass, so that the context-budget gate remains a meaningful signal.
- **Engine maintainer (secondary)** — Wants the startup-context budget to stay honest without recurring manual firefighting.
  - *Story:* As a maintainer, when `AGENTS.md` legitimately grows, I am told to refresh the committed threshold in the same commit (and can do so with one command), so that drift never again blocks the whole team at push time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AGENTS.md trimmed with no loss of clarity:** The redundant `## Worklog Rules` bullet index (744 B duplicating sections of the always-loaded global `AGENTS.md`) is condensed to a concise pointer; `AGENTS.md` drops below the committed threshold and no normative guidance is removed. *Verified by:* measured byte size ≤ threshold and review confirming the pointer still directs readers to the global ruleset.
2. **Threshold refreshed to the post-trim size:** `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` `project_agents` and `total` equal the new `AGENTS.md` byte size; `python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py --repo-root . --include-hidden --thresholds docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` reports no threshold exceeded.
3. **Push gate passes without bypass:** A subsequent `git push` to `dev` succeeds **without** `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`.
4. **Durable guard prevents recurrence:** A committed refresh helper (e.g. `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh`) regenerates the thresholds using the same `measure_context.py` resolution order as `.githooks/pre-push`; a unit test asserts the committed thresholds match the measured startup context surface and fails with the refresh command when stale, so drift is caught locally (by the pre-push unit-test gate) instead of surfacing only as a push-time block.
5. **Guard is fail-open when tooling is absent:** The guard test skips (with a clear reason) when `measure_context.py` is unavailable, mirroring the pre-push hook's documented fail-open behaviour, so environments without the global `context-audit` skill are not broken.
6. **Documentation:** `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (referenced by the pre-push hook but currently missing) documents what the gate measures, why an `AGENTS.md` edit requires a threshold refresh in the same commit, and the exact refresh workflow.
7. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The trim must preserve all normative guidance; only redundant duplication of the always-loaded global ruleset may be removed. If any candidate trim risks losing clarity, stop and ask the producer rather than guessing.
- The context-budget gate must remain meaningful — the guard must **not** silently auto-ratchet the threshold; refreshing stays a deliberate, committed act.
- Reuse the existing measurement tooling (`~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`) and its `--write-thresholds` / `--generate-thresholds` modes rather than reimplementing measurement; keep the guard's path-resolution order consistent with `.githooks/pre-push` (local `skill/context-audit/` first, then the global install).
- `CHANGELOG.md` is out of scope (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline). Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.
- Keep changes surgical: no unrelated `AGENTS.md` rewrites and no speculative threshold-headroom scheme.

## Existing state

- `AGENTS.md` = 46024 B at `dev` HEAD (`4ec45a49`); committed threshold `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` = `{project_agents: 45898, total: 45898}` (exact-match convention).
- Root cause: commit `2283a146` (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU) grew `AGENTS.md` without refreshing the threshold.
- `.githooks/pre-push` (v2, `core.hooksPath=.githooks`) implements the "Context-budget regression gate (F6, SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY)"; it resolves `measure_context.py` from `$repo_root/skill/context-audit/` then `~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/`, and fails open when tooling/thresholds are absent.
- `skill/context-audit/` does **not** exist in this repo, so the hook uses the global install; there is no refresh script, no guard test, and no `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (the hook's error text references that missing path).
- Precedent: **CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR** (same class, 41706 B > 41692 B) was resolved by a threshold refresh; `CG-0MSZ4TN5Z001JADX` delivered commit `9ea973d9` refreshing 43564 B.
- Duplicate: **CG-0MUFAUPI6002P6PE** (`[infra] context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev pushes: AGENTS.md 46024 B > 45898 B threshold`, open, chore/high) describes the identical problem with a fix and ACs — to be closed as a duplicate of this item per producer decision.
- Related but distinct: **CG-0MUECUD5X00558R4** (child of the Test-skill epic CG-0MUDYCJUC009URD6) carries a threshold-refresh AC scoped to its own `AGENTS.md` edit.

## Desired change

1. **Trim `AGENTS.md`** by condensing the `## Worklog Rules` bullet index to a concise pointer (simulated saving ≈ 654 B → ≈ 45370 B), keeping the `### TCE Project Conventions` subsection intact.
2. **Refresh `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`** to the exact post-trim `AGENTS.md` byte size (both `project_agents` and `total`).
3. **Add the durable guard:**
   - `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — resolve `measure_context.py` (same order as the hook) and regenerate the thresholds; print the delta and the resulting values; exit non-zero with guidance if the tooling is unavailable.
   - A unit test (e.g. `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts`) asserting the committed thresholds equal the measured surface, skipping with a clear reason when the tooling is absent.
   - Optionally improve the pre-push hook's failure text to point at the refresh script.
4. **Document the workflow** in a new `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, and reference it from `docs/DEVELOPER.md` where developer tooling is described (per the doc-update policy).
5. **Close CG-0MUFAUPI6002P6PE** as a duplicate of this item (comment linking both).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS.md` — Trim the `## Worklog Rules` bullet index (744 B) to a concise pointer to the global ruleset.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — Refresh `project_agents` and `total` to the post-trim `AGENTS.md` size.
- `scripts/refresh-context-thresholds.sh` — New refresh helper wrapping `measure_context.py --write-thresholds`.
- `tests/scripts/context-budget-thresholds.test.ts` — New guard test asserting committed thresholds match the measured surface (fail-open when tooling absent).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — New documentation for the gate and refresh workflow (fills the missing path referenced by the hook).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — Optional: point the failure message at the refresh script.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Reference the new context-budget documentation from the developer tooling/quality-gates sections.
- `package.json` — Optional: `context:check` / `context:refresh` npm scripts.

## Related work

- **CG-0MUFAUPI6002P6PE** — `[infra] context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev pushes` (open, chore/high) — duplicate of this item; to be closed.
- **CG-0MTCRF0K2006N0HR** — `[infra] context-budget pre-push gate blocks all dev pushes` (completed) — direct precedent; same drift class, resolved by threshold refresh.

# Chore: Document config-driven game catalogue + create per-game build presets

## Problem statement

The config-driven game catalogue (`configs/*.json` presets + `GAMES_CONFIG`)
is only described briefly and in two places (README and the Developer Guide),
with no single authoritative reference covering the preset schema, resolution
order, the `GAME_INFO` convention, or how to author a new preset. The shipped
presets are distribution-oriented (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full`);
none selects a *specific named game*, so a developer cannot build or run, for
example, Main Street in isolation from the launcher checkout.

## Users and user stories

- As a **game developer**, I want to build/run one specific game in isolation so
  I can iterate quickly without pulling in the other games, using
  `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>`.
- As an **engine maintainer**, I want one authoritative document describing how
  build presets are structured, resolved and created, so I can add a preset
  correctly without reverse-engineering the plugin.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the README to keep a concise summary and
  link to the detailed doc, so the high-traffic entry point stays short while
  the full contract is discoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README keeps a concise "Which games does a build include?" section and links
   to a dedicated detailed document (`docs/dev/game-configuration.md`) for full
   details, replacing the current `docs/DEVELOPER.md#config-driven-game-catalogue`
   anchor as the primary reference.
2. The detailed document describes the preset schema in full: the top-level
   `games` array; required `id`, `path`, `scenePath`; optional `adapterPath`,
   `siblingScenePath` and `siblingAdapterPath` (the `src/`-layout sibling
   fields, Option C); the non-schema `$comment` annotation; preset selection
   (`GAMES_CONFIG` preset name or explicit path, default `core-only`); the
   three-step resolution order (`<root>/<scenePath>` →
   `<path>/<siblingScenePath>` → `<path>/<scenePath>`); the always-present
   core-owned Gym; the `GAME_INFO` convention and parsing; and
   validation/failure modes. It explains what each shipped preset (distribution
   and per-game) is and how it is structured — not only one example.
3. A per-game preset exists at `configs/<game-id>.json` for every example game —
   `beleaguered-castle`, `blackjack`, `coloretto`, `feudalism`, `golf`,
   `lost-cities`, `main-street`, `sushi-go` — each containing exactly that one
   game entry (Gym is always added by the plugin).
4. `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id>` selects exactly that game (+ Gym): the generated
   registry for each per-game preset imports the game's scene class and no other
   game, and one representative per-game preset is verified with a real
   `GAMES_CONFIG=<game-id> npm run build`.
5. Unit tests guard every per-game preset: each ships exactly one game, uses the
   sibling `../tce-<id>` path form, resolves to a real scene module with the
   expected scene class, and generates a catalogue containing that game + Gym and
   no other game. Existing distribution-preset and discovery-plugin tests still
   pass.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: the README
   summary section, the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` catalogue section, the new
   `docs/dev/game-configuration.md`, `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`
   where it references `configs/*.json` presets, and the preset/`GAME_INFO`
   doc comment in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (which still lists
   the pre-rename preset names `core-only`, `all` and `sample`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break the existing distribution presets (`core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/
  `deluxe`/`full`) or their tests; per-game presets are additive.
- Presets are data only — no plugin/behaviour change is required (the plugin
  already iterates `games`).
- UK English in all prose.

## Existing state

- Build presets: `configs/{core-only,solo,arcade,deluxe,full}.json`
  (renamed from `core-only/sample/all` in commit `1b6c84b6`).
- Discovery plugin: `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` (`selectConfigPath`,
  `loadGamesConfig`, `discoverGames`, `renderGameRegistryModule`,
  `selectedGameIds`).
- Tests: `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` (a `PRESET_GAMES` map),
  `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts`.
- Docs: `README.md` ("Which games does a build include?"), `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  ("Config-Driven Game Catalogue"), `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- Known doc drift: the plugin's header doc comment
  (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) still names the pre-rename presets
  `core-only`, `all` and `sample`; correct it to the shipped
  `core-only`/`solo`/`arcade`/`deluxe`/`full` set.
- Deployment note: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` currently builds the default
  (`core-only`) preset — covered by the separate work item CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Desired change

Add eight per-game presets (`configs/<game-id>.json`), add a dedicated
`docs/dev/game-configuration.md` reference, trim/link the README section to it,
and extend the preset tests to cover the per-game set.

## Key Files

- `configs/<game-id>.json` — eight new per-game presets (one game entry each).
- `docs/dev/game-configuration.md` — new authoritative reference for the preset
  schema, resolution, `GAME_INFO` convention and authoring steps.
- `README.md` — concise summary + link to the new doc.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — point the catalogue section at the new doc; keep the
  workflow summary.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — cross-reference the per-game presets
  alongside the existing `configs/*.json` mention.
- `tests/scripts/distribution-presets.test.ts` — extend `PRESET_GAMES` (or add a
  per-game guard) for the eight per-game presets.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — doc comment cross-reference only
  (no behaviour change expected).

## Related work

- CG-0MTRO6Y2N009B9CF — Config-driven game discovery (Vite plugin + configs/).
- CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC — Launcher distribution with configs/ presets (solo/
  arcade/deluxe/full).
- CG-0MTRO7BFQ003IN2X — Documentation for the multi-repo workflow.
- CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1 — Deploy full engine with all games via `GAMES_CONFIG=all`
  (deployment follow-on).
- CG-0MLVJR7JI0YF87IN — Game Selector: Fix card layout for 4+ games (completed;
  the selector must render the growing per-preset catalogue cleanly).
- CG-0MSKVOSW3004HZVB — Verify full suite green with documented deps (completed;
  establishes the test baseline this change must keep green).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** per-game presets are named `configs/<game-id>.json` (so
  `GAMES_CONFIG=main-street`), matching the `id` used everywhere else.
- **Assumption:** the existing distribution presets are kept as-is; per-game
  presets are additive (`solo.json` remains a golf distribution preset even
  though `configs/golf.json` also selects golf).
- **Risk (low):** preset proliferation / maintenance (13 presets). Mitigated by
  a test that derives the per-game set from the game list rather than hand-listing.
- **Risk (low):** doc drift between README, DEVELOPER.md and the new doc.
  Mitigated by making the new doc the single detailed reference and linking from
  both.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the `deploy.yml` `GAMES_CONFIG` change is out of scope
  here and tracked by CG-0MUGSGH7Q002NOA1.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview questions were required. Requirements were stated explicitly by
  the operator: (a) keep the README configuration section brief and link to a
  separate document; (b) the separate document must explain how configurations
  are created and structured — not just describe one example preset; (c) create
  one configuration per game so each game can be built in isolation.
- The preset renaming to `solo/arcade/deluxe/full` (commit `1b6c84b6`) landed
  during this session; this brief reflects the post-rename state.
data.title: Document config-driven game catalogue + create per-game build presets

# Feature: Per-game repos use `src/` source root with alias-based core imports (Option C)

Part of epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Follow-on refinement of the F4 game-repo scaffold.

## Goal

As a game developer I can clone a `tce-<game>` repo and find that game's source at the repo-root `src/` directory, with every engine import going through the `@core-engine/*` (and `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) path aliases, so that the repo has an idiomatic layout and does not rely on the `src -> ../tableau-card-engine-core/src` compatibility symlink or fragile `../../src/**` relative imports.

## Problem

The F4 scaffold keeps the game nested at `example-games/<game>/` and creates a `src` symlink into the core checkout. 319 game-source imports use `../../src/**` and only resolve because the game sits exactly two levels below the repo root. This is fragile, non-idiomatic, and blocks moving the game source to `src/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Decision record exists (child C1) fixing the per-game layout (`src/**` or `src/<game>/**`), how `scripts/`, `example-games/gym`, shared assets and test helpers resolve from `src/`, and the `scenePath` contract for monorepo-local vs sibling-repo contexts.
2. A scaffolded `tce-<game>` checkout has its game source under `src/`, contains no `src` symlink to the core, and `npm run build` + `npm test -- --project unit` succeed.
3. No game-repo source or test imports core through a `../../src/**` relative specifier; a test/lint guards this invariant.
4. The launcher (`configs/*.json` presets + `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) resolves game scenes in both the flat monorepo (`example-games/<game>/…`) and the `src/` sibling game-repo layout; the 1-game (`solo`) and all-games (`full`) presets both build.
5. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md` describe the new per-game layout.

## Constraints

- The monorepo/launcher flat layout may stay `example-games/<game>/`; only per-game repos change to `src/`. C1 may override this if a uniform layout proves cleaner.
- The producer gate on F4 still applies: no GitHub repo creation or push.
- Engine imports must resolve via `tsconfig.json` `paths` + Vite `resolve.alias`; no new npm publication of the engine.

## Children

- C1 Decide per-game `src/` layout, import contract and preset resolution
- C2 Codemod game source + tests off `../../src/**` to engine aliases
- C3 Extraction/scaffold/repo-layout emit the `src/` layout
- C4 Discovery plugin + launcher presets resolve `src/` sibling layouts
- C5 Update game docs and verify per-game tsc/build/unit

## Goal

As a game-repo consumer I have a signed-off decision record so that C2–C5 implement one agreed layout instead of diverging.

## Scope

Produce the decision record for Option C. It must fix:

1. **Per-game root shape** — game source at `src/**` (flat, single game) or `src/<game>/**`. State why.
2. **Where the game's non-source trees live** — tests (repo `tests/**` vs `src/**/*.test.ts`), the replay-adapter script, game-local scripts, docs, layout JSON.
3. **How the remaining core symlinks resolve from `src/`** — `scripts -> core/scripts` (replay framework), `example-games/gym -> core/…/gym`, `tests/helpers -> core/tests/helpers`, `core -> ../tableau-card-engine-core`, and shared `public/assets/**`. Decide which remain symlinks, which become aliases, and which imports become `core/...`.
4. **Import contract** — the exact alias form for engine imports (`@core-engine/*` etc.) and, where no alias exists (e.g. replay framework), whether to add an alias or keep a symlink-backed path.
5. **`scenePath` contract across contexts** — how `configs/*.json` presets express the scene path so the discovery plugin resolves it both in the flat monorepo (`example-games/<game>/…`) and in a `src/`-layout sibling repo. Decide between a per-context field (e.g. `siblingScenePath`), per-repo presets, or path probing, and record the migration for the committed presets.
6. **Interaction with F4/F5/F7** — note that F4/F5 outputs are reworked and F7 verification must be re-run after this feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Decision record committed under `docs/dev/` and cross-linked from `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.

3. The record enumerates the concrete per-context `scenePath` values for `configs/full.json` (monorepo) and a sample game repo's `configs/game.json`.

- Notes feeding C2/C3/C4

# Task: Create the nine `tce-*` GitHub repositories and push extracted history

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,
   `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`,
   `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`.
2. Each repository's default branch contains the extracted,
   history-preserving tree in the F9 `src/` layout (extraction via
   `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, scaffold via `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`):
   the core repo holds the engine + Gym + launcher shell and **no games**; each
   game repo has its source at repo-root `src/` and wires the engine as a
   `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
3. From a **fresh remote clone**, `git clone --recurse-submodules <game-repo>`
   followed by `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds for at least **golf** and **main-street**.
4. The launcher can compose a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings (spot
   check: the `solo` and `full` presets build against fresh clones).
5. Evidence is recorded on this work item: the extraction commit count per repo
   (as F1 did) and the source monorepo commit SHA the nine repos were extracted
   from.
6. No CI pipeline and no npm publication are added (out of scope, per the epic
   constraints).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (In practice:
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 currently says the remotes are
   *not* created; `README.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md` clone guidance must document
   the `--recurse-submodules` workflow.)
8. Validation for the change: the extraction/scaffold unit suites
   (`tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`,
   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) pass, and the published remotes
   are validated by the fresh-clone checks in AC3/AC4.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No CI pipeline and no npm publication (epic constraint).
- Never rewrite the source monorepo: extraction always operates on a clone
  (`git clone --no-local`); the monorepo `main` is never pushed to directly.
- `git filter-repo` is required and is **not currently installed** on this host
  (`pip install git-filter-repo` per
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`).
- GitHub org write access is required; the authenticated account
  (`SorraTheOrc`) is an **admin** of the `TheWizardsCode` org, so credentials are
  available and creating repos is permitted.
- Remotes use SSH (`git@github.com:...`), consistent with `repo-layout.json`.
- Repos are created once, after F9, in the final `src/` layout.
- **Visibility:** all nine repos are created **public** (producer answer, Q1).
- **Published refs:** push only `dev` plus `main` seeded from it; do **not**
  push the monorepo's feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` tags (Q4).
- **Source revision:** extract from the current `dev` HEAD and record its SHA
  as evidence (producer answer, Q3).

## Existing state

- **F1** delivered `scripts/extract-repos.sh` +
  `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (history-preserving extraction; verified
  locally: 852 core commits, 23–995 per game).
- **F2** delivered the core-engine repo tree (locally verified standalone).
- **F4** delivered `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and local per-game checkouts;
  GitHub remote creation was explicitly out of scope (producer gate).
- **F9** reworked per-game repos to repo-root `src/` with alias-only engine
  imports.
- **F5/F7** delivered the launcher distribution and integration verification
  against local sibling checkouts.
- Verified as part of intake: **none** of the nine remotes exist on GitHub
  (`gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/<repo>` → 404).
- The `solo` preset is golf-only; the `full` preset covers all eight games.

## Desired change

Extract all nine repos from the monorepo at the current `dev` HEAD, scaffold the
eight game repos, commit, create the nine GitHub repositories, push each repo's
history to its default branch, and record the per-repo commit counts plus the
source SHA as evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` — drives `--target <name>` extraction for the nine
  targets; may need an end-to-end "create remote + push" helper or documented
  commands.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — scaffolds each extracted game checkout.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — source of truth for names/remotes/paths
  (already final; read-only for this task).
- `configs/solo.json`, `configs/full.json` — spot-check sibling composition.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "GitHub remotes are not created in
  this phase" must be updated to the published state.
- `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — clone-with-submodules instructions.
- `.gitmodules` (per game repo) — `core` submodule wiring.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Visibility / branch model / source revision** — resolved by the producer
  (public; `dev`→`main` with `main` seeded once; current `dev` HEAD with SHA
  recorded); see Appendix Q1–Q3.
- **Published refs** — the filtered clone inherits ~150 branches and 17
  `v0.1.x` tags; publishing only `dev`+`main` avoids stale-branch and cross-repo
  tag confusion (Appendix Q4).
- **History** — preserved as content/provenance, but retained commits receive
  **new SHAs** (inherent to a filtered subset); see Appendix Q3 research.
- `git filter-repo` is not installed on this host — a blocker for real runs
  (fine for `--dry-run`).
- The extraction renames `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` (`--path-rename`) and
  the scaffold rewrites intra-test paths; both history-preserving behaviours were
  verified by F9.
- **Scope-creep risk**: switching the launcher monorepo to point its
  `.gitmodules` at the new remote submodules, adding CI, or publishing npm
  packages are **out of scope**; record any such opportunity as a separate
  child/discovered work item rather than expanding this task.
- Assumption: the agent creates the repos and pushes (this item is the
  authorisation the F4 producer gate deferred).

## Related work

- **F1** *Design architecture & extraction script with history*
  (CG-0MTRO6P18003AZIZ) — the extraction script and repo-layout contract.
- **F2** *Create core-engine repository* (CG-0MTRO6SZH006EBVN) — core tree.
- **F4** *Per-game repos as single-game launchers (local scaffold)*
  (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) — parent split; producer gate deferred remotes.
- **F5** *Launcher distribution with configs/ presets*
  (CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC) — the `solo`/`full` presets used for AC4.
- **F7** *Integration verification — full build & test suite*
  (CG-0MTRO7ECL006ID7J) — local sibling verification precedent.
- **F9** *Per-game repos use src/ source root with alias-based core imports*
  (CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME) — the final layout this task must publish.
- **Epic** *REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own
  projects* (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17).
- Reference: `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`,
  `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MRPH9YF0008QIZY** – Document TCE game-development best practices as an agent skill (completed)
- **CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0** – Add runtime audio synthesis for dynamic SFX (WebAudio/Tone.js) (completed)
- **CG-0MM03ITUF1SKCSOZ** – Fix Golf browser test failures in CI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+116 more)
- `AGENTS.md` – matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+102 more)
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — matched: 0muh0ntrg007gdme, architecture, beleaguered, blackjack, build (+96 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (visibility) — ANSWERED.** Should the nine new GitHub repositories be
  **public** or **private**? **Answer (producer):** **public**. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Adopt `gh repo create --public` for all nine.
- **Q2 (branch model) — ANSWERED.** Which branch should be the **default** and
  what should be pushed? **Answer (producer):** keep the TCE `dev` → `main`
  flow — seed `main` once from the extracted `dev` history (initial
  publication), then continue dev→main promotion via the ship skill. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Options considered: (a) `dev` as default;
  (b) seed `main` once then dev→main; (c) single `main`. Answer = (b).
- **Q3 (source revision) — ANSWERED (condition satisfied).** Extract from the
  current `dev` HEAD (record the SHA), or pin to a stable/tagged commit?
  **Answer (producer):** current `dev` HEAD as recommended, **conditional on
  history being maintained** — the producer asked “will this maintain history?
  Can we maintain history?”.
  - **Research (history preservation):** **Yes.** `git filter-repo` retains
    every commit that touched each repo's selected paths, including author,
    date, message and ancestry, so per-file `git log`/`git blame` continuity is
    preserved; the Option C `example-games/<game>/ → src/` rename is applied in
    the same filter pass, so history follows the file to its new path, and the
    result is pushed verbatim (nothing squashed). Evidence:
    `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §“History preservation”;
    `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (`--path-rename` + `--path` filters); F1’s
    recorded retention counts; local probe `git log -- example-games/golf` =
    103 commits, `git log -- example-games/main-street` = 668 commits; the
    GolfScene.ts `--follow` chain reaches its first commit.
  - **Caveat 1 (SHAs change):** because each repo is a filtered *subset*, the
    retained commits are rewritten and receive **new SHAs** — history content
    and provenance are preserved, hash identity with the monorepo is not.
    (This is inherent to any subset split, including `git subtree`.)
  - **Caveat 2 (what we publish):** the extraction clone inherits the
    monorepo's ~150 branches and 17 `v0.1.x` tags; publish only the intended
    refs (see Q4).
  - **Conclusion:** the condition holds — proceed with current `dev` HEAD and
    record `git rev-parse dev` as evidence. Source: interactive reply,
    2026-09-26.
- **Q4 (published refs) — DECISION RECORDED (producer informed via session
  summary; not re-blocked).** Which refs are pushed to the nine new remotes?
  **Recommended and adopted:** push only the intended long-lived branches —
  `dev` plus `main` seeded from it — and do **not** publish the monorepo's
  feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` release tags (those are engine-wide
  and would be misleading on per-game repos). Tag the new repos from their own
  first release. Rationale: matches the `dev`→`main` model in Q2 and avoids
  150+ stale branches / cross-repo tag confusion. Source: agent recommendation
  recorded 2026-09-26; producer may override.

*(Resolved 2026-09-26. This Appendix is updated idempotently; new open items
would be marked OPEN QUESTION.)*

---

**Plan: changelog** — 2026-09-26, agent `plan`, session
`herdr-1790434710-2326366-1278`: decomposed this item into six child tasks

# Intake Brief: Beleaguered Castle — cards cannot be selected to move them (CG-0MUHKD7S8007EEAC)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Fix a reproducible card-selection defect in Beleaguered Castle: the first click immediately after the deal completes is silently dropped because newly registered top cards are not yet hit-testable, and harden selection feedback so a click always produces visible, reliable selection regardless of renderer.

## Problem Statement

Operators report that in Beleaguered Castle they "cannot select any cards to move them". Investigation confirms at least one reproducible selection defect — the first click after the deal animation completes is ignored — plus two aggravating factors (no visible selection highlight under the Canvas renderer, and only the top card of each column being interactive). The result is that a player's click can appear to do nothing, making the game feel unresponsive or unplayable.

## Users

- **Solitaire player:** Wants to click a card and immediately see it selected, then click a destination to move it, without having to click twice or guess whether the click registered.
  - *"As a player, I want my first click on a card after the deal to select it, so the game feels responsive and I can plan moves confidently."*
- **QA / playtester:** Needs deterministic, reproducible interaction behaviour so selection bugs can be captured in browser tests and not recur.
  - *"As a tester, I want a browser regression test that fails if the first post-deal click is dropped, so this class of bug is caught automatically."*
- **Engine developer:** Wants the fix to live in the shared interaction layer (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts` / `HandView`) where the registration race originates, rather than as a game-local workaround.
  - *"As an engine developer, I want newly registered draggables to be hit-testable immediately, so every game using the shared module benefits."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **First post-deal click always selects:** In the natural (non-reduced-motion) boot flow — choose variant → deal completes → immediate first click on a tableau top card — the column is selected on the very first click, 100% of runs (no dropped click, no retry required). Verified by a new browser test that repeats the sequence across multiple boots/seeds.
2. **Selection is visibly indicated in all renderers:** A selected top card shows a persistent, distinct highlight under both WebGL and Canvas renderers (BC currently uses raw `setTint()`, which is a no-op in Phaser 4 Canvas; the shared HandView Canvas-compatible tint-overlay approach must be used or equivalent).
3. **End-to-end click-to-move works from a clean natural boot:** From a fresh natural boot, selecting a top card and then clicking a legal destination (foundation or tableau column) executes exactly one undoable move, with the highlight and selection state clearing/reset appropriately.
4. **Double-click / same-card deselect unaffected:** Clicking an already-selected card deselects it, and clicking a different valid source re-selects, preserving the documented click-to-move contract.
5. **Regression tests:** New browser test(s) under `tests/beleaguered-castle/` cover the first-click and click-to-move flows in the natural boot path; the existing drag/click coexistence tests continue to pass.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `help-content.json` if the interaction contract changes, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve dual-input:** Both drag-and-drop and click-to-move must continue to work simultaneously; the click-vs-drag threshold (`dragDistanceThreshold`) behaviour must be preserved.
- **No behavioural regression for other games:** Any change to the shared drag-drop module (`src/ui/dragDrop.ts`) or `HandView` must not break Main Street, Golf, Coloretto, the Gym, or other consumers. Prefer a fix at the shared layer that is additive and backward-compatible.
- **Reduced-motion and replay/test paths:** The reduced-motion (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and replay paths must remain functional; the fix must not depend on animations having run.
- **Licensing:** All code/assets remain permissively licensed (MIT/Apache/CC0).
- **Scope:** Fix the selection/move reliability bug; do not add a hint-system overhaul or change game rules.

## Existing State

- **Selection logic:** `BeleagueredCastleScene.handleCardClick()` → `selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` implement click-to-select. `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.makeDraggable()` attaches the top card's `pointerdown` → `onCardClick`, and registers the top card as a draggable via the shared `DragDropManager.registerDraggable()`.
- **Interaction gate:** `interactionBlocked` returns true while `!dealComplete || gameEnded || autoCompleting`; `dealComplete` is set in the renderer's `onDealComplete`, which then calls `makeDraggable()`.
- **Registration race (confirmed):** Immediately after `makeDraggable()`, the top-card sprites are present in `scene.input` as interactive but sit in the input plugin's pending-insertion queue (`_pendingInsertion`) and are **not** yet in the active hit-test list (`_list`). A click arriving before the next input `preUpdate` is silently ignored. Diagnostic evidence: `sprite.input=true`, `input.enabled=true`, `inList=false`, `inPending=true`; the first click failed in 3 of 5 natural boots, while a retry (or a ≥~500 ms settle delay) always succeeded.
- **Renderer highlight:** `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` use raw `setTint()` / `clearTint()`. Per the `HandView` documentation, `setTint()` is a no-op in Phaser 4's Canvas renderer, so no selection highlight is visible when the game falls back to Canvas.
- **Only top cards interactive:** Covered (non-top) tableau cards are not interactive by design; clicking them does nothing. This is intentional but may read as "cannot select" to a new player.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` covers drag-to-foundation/tableau, illegal/out-of-zone snap-back, reduced-motion behaviour, and a click-vs-drag coexistence test (`click without drag still selects a column`). That suite boots in reduced-motion test mode (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`) and does not exercise the natural deal-then-click timing, which is where the race manifests.
- **Deployment:** The game uses `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL with Canvas fallback) via `createCardGame`. `origin/main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling (differences are import-alias refactors and `GAME_INFO` metadata).

## Desired Change

1. **Eliminate the post-deal click race** so the first click after the deal always selects. Investigate the correct fix at the shared layer — e.g. ensure newly registered draggables/interactive top cards are flushed into the input hit-test list (or registered earlier / re-registered on the next tick) before interaction is considered available — rather than masking it with a game-local delay. Keep the fix additive and safe for all `DragDropManager`/`HandView` consumers.
2. **Make selection feedback renderer-agnostic:** replace BC's raw `setTint()` selection highlight with the shared Canvas-compatible mechanism (e.g. HandView's tint-overlay helper) or an equivalent persistent outline that renders in both WebGL and Canvas.
3. **Add natural-flow regression tests:** a browser test that boots without `__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`, dismisses the variant popup, waits for the deal, and asserts the immediate first click selects; plus a click-to-move end-to-end assertion. Reuse the existing BC drag-test helpers where possible.
4. **Verify the end-to-end contract** (select → destination click → one undoable move) and document the interaction as tested.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts` — `makeDraggable()` registration timing; `selectColumn()`/`deselectColumn()` highlight mechanism.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleScene.ts` — `handleCardClick()`, `selectColumn()`, `wireInput()`, `interactionBlocked`, deal-complete wiring.
- `src/ui/dragDrop.ts` — `registerDraggable()` `setInteractive` / input-list timing; potential shared-layer fix.
- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Canvas-compatible tint-overlay helper to reuse for BC selection.
- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` — extend/add natural-flow first-click + click-to-move regression tests.
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/help-content.json` — update only if the interaction contract changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks
- **Narrow-window vs persistent symptom:** The confirmed first-click race is short-lived (one input `preUpdate`); on a foregrounded 60 fps browser it is ~16 ms. The operator's "cannot select any cards" may be a broader symptom (perception, device, throttled frames, Canvas fallback). Mitigation: fix the confirmed defect, harden highlight visibility, and add an explicit open question for the operator; treat any additional scenario as a linked follow-up rather than expanding this item indefinitely.
- **Shared-module regression:** Changing `DragDropManager`/`HandView` input timing could affect Main Street, Golf, Coloretto and the Gym. Mitigation: keep the change additive, run the affected games' browser suites, and prefer a fix that does not alter existing drag semantics.
- **Test flakiness:** Timing-based browser tests can flake. Mitigation: assert on deterministic scene state (`selectedCol`, `moveCount`) and repeat the boot sequence across seeds; avoid wall-clock sleeps where possible.
- **Canvas fallback coverage:** Headless CI can force Canvas; verify the highlight fix visually/structurally in both renderer modes.
- **Scope creep:** A broader "make every card clickable" or "rework selection UX" redesign would expand scope. Record such ideas as linked follow-up work items instead.

### Assumptions
- The operator is running the current `dev` code in a standard browser (mouse input); the deployed `main` build is functionally identical for BC input.
- The first-click race is a genuine defect worth fixing regardless of whether it fully explains the operator's report.
- Reduced-motion and replay modes must remain unaffected by the fix.

## Related Work

- **Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MLSDWFLT1WB6IEB)** [completed]: The epic that built the game, including click-to-move, drag-and-drop, undo/redo, and auto-move.
- **Click-to-Move Card Input (CG-0MLTFE68N1TONFIE)** [completed]: Introduced the click-to-move interaction contract this bug affects.
- **Highlight for selected card (CG-0MOJ44AXO006HFAS)** [completed]: Prior critical selection-feedback bug (market cards); establishes the project's expectation of a persistent, visible selection marker and Canvas-safe rendering.
- **Refactor Beleaguered Castle to use the core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKSLDXQ008F5Y3)** [completed]: Moved BC onto the shared `DragDropManager` where the registration timing originates.
- **Add drag-drop browser tests for Beleaguered Castle (CG-0MSN4C4LI007VVGK)** [completed]: The existing BC interaction test suite that will be extended.
- **Reusable core-engine drag-drop module (CG-0MSKT0NQP0018KK6)** [completed]: The shared module whose `registerDraggable()` timing is implicated.
- **Bugs in Beleaguered Castle HandView/PileView migration** (related completed items under the BC epic) — context on recent BC interaction refactors.

### Related work (automated report)

Searched Worklog and repository files for keywords derived from the report (beleaguered, castle, cards, click, deal, first, select, move, ignored, cannot). The automated `find-related` pass returned 3 related items and 3 repository matches:

- **CG-0MLTFCTNK10RQ41T** – Beleaguered Castle Game Logic (completed): the game-logic foundation underlying move legality used by selection/move.
- **CG-0MSRGV53I009BKKR** – Held-event play burst feedback (completed): interaction-feedback precedent in the codebase.
- **CG-0MUF6LBW600657B2** – [test-failure] skills-extensions-tracking.test.ts ignore check is vacuous (open): unrelated test-infrastructure item surfaced by keyword overlap; no dependency.
- Repository file matches: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (keyword overlap only — no code paths implicated).

The manual Related Work list above is the authoritative set; the automated matches are broad and mostly keyword-driven.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does the failure happen on the very first click after the deal, or on every click?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Investigation could only reproduce a *first-click-after-deal* drop; subsequent clicks succeeded. Awaiting operator confirmation of whether their experience is intermittent (first click) or total (all clicks).
- **Q: Are you playing in WebGL or does your browser fall back to Canvas?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Canvas fallback would additionally hide the `setTint` selection highlight, which could read as "not selected". The game defaults to `Phaser.AUTO` (WebGL preferred).
- **Q: Is this the local dev build or the deployed `main` build?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). `main` and `dev` are functionally identical for BC input handling, so the same defect is expected in both.
- **Q: Are you clicking the fully visible top card of a column, or a partly covered card?** — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (operator). Only the top card of each column is interactive by design; covered cards intentionally do nothing.

## Suggested Next Step

Confirm the operator's exact scenario via the open questions above, then implement the confirmed fix (input-registration flush + Canvas-safe selection highlight) with natural-flow browser regression tests.

## Problem

Beleaguered Castle uses raw `setTint()` / `clearTint()` in `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.selectColumn()` and `deselectColumn()` to highlight the selected column's top card. `setTint()` is a no-op in Phaser 4's Canvas renderer, so the selection highlight is invisible when the game falls back to Canvas.

## Fix

Create a canvas-compatible selection highlight helper that renders a semi-transparent overlay rectangle behind `setTint()` (for WebGL compatibility). The helper should:

1. Create a rectangle matching the sprite's dimensions, positioned at the sprite's location, with a configurable tint colour and alpha.
2. Use depth `sprite.depth + 0.01` so it renders just above the card.
3. On deselect, destroy the overlay rectangle and clear any `setTint()`.

Replace `BeleagueredCastleRenderer.selectColumn()` / `deselectColumn()` to use this helper instead of raw `setTint()`.

**Reference:** `HandView._setCardTint()` already implements this pattern (tint + overlay rectangle) — extract the overlay logic into a reusable utility.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A selected top card shows a visible highlight under both WebGL and Canvas renderers.
2. The highlight is persistent (doesn't disappear on refresh/redraw).
3. Deselect removes the highlight cleanly (no orphaned rectangles).
4. Existing drag-to-move tests continue to pass.

## Key Files

- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleRenderer.ts` — `selectColumn()`, `deselectColumn()`
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/scenes/BeleagueredCastleConstants.ts` — `SELECTION_TINT`

## References

- CG-0MUHKD7S8007EEAC: Parent work item (Beleaguered Castle selection fix)
- CG-0MOJ44AXO006HFAS: Prior selection-feedback bug (Canvas-safe rendering precedent)

## Problem

The existing BC drag tests run in reduced-motion test mode (`__BC_TEST_REDUCED_MOTION__`), which skips the deal animation. They don't exercise the natural deal-then-click timing where the first-click race manifests.

## Fix

Add browser tests in `tests/beleaguered-castle/` that:

### Test 1: First click after deal selects (first-click race)

- Boot game with `Phaser.CANVAS` renderer (forces Canvas to also validate the selection highlight fix).
- Clear persistent storage (avoid resume overlay).
- Set the variant preference to `'classic'` (skip variant popup).
- Wait for deal to complete (poll `scene.isDealComplete()` and all tableau columns populated).
- **Immediately** dispatch a mousedown+mouseup on the top card of column 0 (no artificial delay).
- Assert `scene.selectedCol === 0`.
- Repeat across 3 different seeds to verify deterministic behaviour.

### Test 2: Click-to-move end-to-end

- Same boot flow as Test 1.
- Click a top card (column 0) to select it.
- Click a legal destination (e.g., foundation or tableau column).
- Assert the move count incremented by exactly 1.
- Assert the card moved to the destination pile.
- Assert `scene.selectedCol === null` (selection cleared after move).
- Assert `scene.getUndoManager().canUndo()` is true.

### Test 3: Same-card deselect

- Boot game.
- Click a top card to select it.
- Click the same card again.
- Assert `scene.selectedCol === null` (deselected).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three new tests pass consistently (no flakiness).
2. Tests boot in CANVAS mode to validate both the hit-test fix and the Canvas-visible selection highlight.
3. Existing drag tests continue to pass.
4. Tests use deterministic state assertions (moveCount, selectedCol) rather than wall-clock sleeps.

## Key Files

- `tests/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleDrag.browser.test.ts` — extend with new test cases
- `example-games/beleaguered-castle/BeleagueredCastleVariant.ts` — variant persistence helpers

## References

- CG-0MUHKD7S8007EEAC: Parent work item (Beleaguered Castle selection fix)

## Problem statement

The Tableau Card Engine ships pre-1.0 builds (currently `v0.1.17`), but nothing in the UI signals that players are using an ALPHA build. Every game screen, the game-selector menu, and the Help/Settings panes should show a brightly coloured red **ALPHA** badge carrying the current version number, so users and testers always know they are on an unreleased ALPHA build.

## Users

- **Players / testers** — "When I open any game, I can immediately see that this is an ALPHA build and which version I'm on, so I know to report issues and can quote the exact version."
- **Release manager / producer** — "I can visually confirm from any screen that the deployed build is an ALPHA build and that the running version matches the release."
- **Developers** — "The badge is rendered by one shared helper, so adding a new game scene automatically gets the ALPHA banner with no per-game work."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A bright red **ALPHA** badge displaying the current version string (from `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, i.e. the build-time `__APP_VERSION__`) is rendered **stacked above/over the title** on every Example Game scene and every Gym demo scene, delivered through the shared scene-title helper (`createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`), so no per-game bespoke code is required. The one remaining bespoke title call site — `BlackjackScene`, which draws `'Blackjack'` with its own `scene.add.text` — is migrated to `createSceneTitle()` so no bespoke title rendering remains.
2. The same red ALPHA + version badge appears stacked above/over the one-off title on the Game Selector menu screen.
3. The SettingsPanel title shows the badge stacked above/over it, and HelpPanel gains a compact **"Help" + ALPHA badge** header at the top of its content (HelpPanel currently has no title heading).
4. The badge's version text equals `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; the existing muted version labels on the menu (top-right) and settings (bottom-left) remain unchanged.
5. The badge renders correctly (legible, no clipping, no overlap with the top-left `Menu` button, the top-right HUD controls, or the existing version label) at the fixed 1280×720 design resolution used by every surface (`GAME_W` × `GAME_H`, `Phaser.Scale.FIT` with `CENTER_BOTH`); automated tests cover the shared badge helper and assert a badge showing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is created on each surface (Example Game / Gym header, Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared-helper first.** All scene/game/Gym titles already route through `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`); extend those rather than patching individual scenes. The Game Selector title, `SettingsPanel` title, and `HelpPanel` header are separate one-off call sites.
- **Reuse the version source.** Do not access `__APP_VERSION__` directly — import the existing `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` / style constants from `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` so version handling stays in one place.
- **No new assets / permissive only.** Red badge must be drawn with Phaser primitives (rectangle + text); no new image assets, no new dependencies.
- **Do not remove existing version labels** (producer decision Q3a) — the badge is additive.
- **Reduced motion.** The badge is static (no animation), so it is inherently reduced-motion safe; do not add motion.
- **Canvas headroom.** Scene titles sit at `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`; a badge stacked *above* the title has little vertical room. Option (c) permits overlaying/overlapping the title's upper edge; the chosen geometry must remain legible and must not collide with the top-left `Menu` button or top-right HUD controls.
- **SLL requirement.** Positioning must respect the project's SLL/no-hardcoded-pixel rule where practical; the title helpers already own their fixed header geometry, so the badge should be defined relative to the title it decorates.

## Existing state

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — `createSceneTitle()` (centred title at `GAME_W/2`, `SCENE_HEADER_Y = 14`) and `createSceneHeader()` (title + `Menu` button). Used by all Example Game renderers/scenes and `GymSceneBase.initHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` (`v<version>` from build-time `__APP_VERSION__`), `VERSION_COLOR`, `VERSION_ALPHA`, `VERSION_DEPTH`, `createVersionLabel()`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — one-off bold title `'Tableau Card Engine'` at `(GAME_W/2, 30)` with a subtitle; version label already rendered top-right below the GitHub icon.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — one-off `'Settings'` title at `(panelWidth/2, PADDING + 30)`.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — sections rendered in a scrollable content container; **no** title heading today.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — `initHeader(title)` delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.

## Desired change

Add a shared `createAlphaBadge(scene, opts)` factory (in `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` or a new `src/ui/AlphaBadge.ts`) that renders a bright red badge containing `ALPHA` and `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`, positioned stacked above/over a given title (with an explicit anchor/y so callers control overlap). Wire it into `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` by default (with an opt-out flag) so every Example Game and Gym scene inherits it, then add it explicitly to the Game Selector title, the SettingsPanel title, and a new compact HelpPanel header. Keep the existing muted version labels.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Extend `tests/ui/SceneHeader.test.ts` with failing unit tests for `createAlphaBadge()`: bright red fill, `ALPHA` + `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` text, anchor/overlap geometry relative to the decorated title, and the opt-out flag.
2. Add per-surface presence tests — `tests/ui/GameSelectorScene.test.ts`, `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVersion.browser.test.ts`, and a new `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts`.
3. Implement `createAlphaBadge()` plus the default-on wiring in `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()`; export the factory and constants from `src/ui/index.ts`.
4. Wire the one-off surfaces (Game Selector title, SettingsPanel title, HelpPanel header) and migrate `BlackjackScene` to `createSceneTitle()`.
5. Update documentation (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Build-Time Version Injection" section, `README.md`) and code comments.
6. Verify: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/`, then the unit profile before any push (`npm test -- --project unit` + `npm run build`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — Add `createAlphaBadge()`; render the badge from `createSceneTitle()` / `createSceneHeader()` (default on, opt-out config).
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — Reuse `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; add red-badge style constants (or a `createAlphaBadge` export here if it fits better).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Tableau Card Engine'` title.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Stack the badge above/over the `'Settings'` title.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — Add a compact `Help` + ALPHA badge header at the top of the content area.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — Export the new badge factory/constants.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — Verify the inherited header path renders the badge (likely no change if `createSceneHeader()` handles it).
- `tests/ui/*.test.ts` / `*.browser.test.ts` — Unit/integration tests for the badge helper and per-surface presence.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/SceneHeader.ts` — add `createAlphaBadge()` and default-on wiring in `createSceneTitle()` (opt-out on `SceneTitleConfig`) / `createSceneHeader()`.
- `src/ui/versionDisplay.ts` — reuse `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT`; red badge colour and geometry constants.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — stack the badge above/over the `'Tableau Card Engine'` title.
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — stack the badge above/over the `'Settings'` title.
- `src/ui/HelpPanel.ts` — compact `Help` + ALPHA badge header at the top of the content area.
- `src/ui/index.ts` — export the badge factory and constants.
- `example-games/blackjack/scenes/BlackjackScene.ts` — migrate the bespoke `'Blackjack'` title to `createSceneTitle()` so it inherits the badge.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSceneBase.ts` — verification only; `initHeader()` already delegates to `createSceneHeader()`.
- `tests/ui/SceneHeader.test.ts` — unit tests for `createAlphaBadge()` and the helper default behaviour.
- `tests/ui/GameSelectorScene.test.ts` — assert the badge is created on the menu title.
- `tests/ui/SettingsPanelVersion.browser.test.ts` — assert the badge renders on the settings title alongside the existing label.
- `tests/ui/HelpPanel.test.ts` — assert the new `Help` + ALPHA badge header exists (new test file).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — update the "Build-Time Version Injection" section for the badge and helper wiring.
- `./README.md` — document the ALPHA badge on all screens.

**Note:** Paths above are the planned touch points; the `tests/ui/*.test.ts` / `*.browser.test.ts` glob in the predicted list is indicative of the coverage to add.

## Related work

- `CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W` — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed) — established the version-label pattern this item extends.
- `CG-0MSHQPDQ80015RF7` — Move the version number on the menu page below the GitHub logo (completed) — current version-label placement.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — top-of-canvas clipping.** Stacking a badge above a title at `y = 14` risks clipping at the canvas edge or colliding with the `Menu` button. *Mitigation:* define the badge geometry relative to the title with a small controlled overlap (per option (c)), and verify at supported canvas sizes; add a browser test/visual check.
- **Risk — banner overload.** Adding a badge to *all* surfaces (Q2a) could add visual noise to 30+ Gym dev scenes. *Mitigation:* keep the badge compact and consistent; it is intentional per the producer decision.
- **Risk — duplicate version indicators.** Existing muted labels plus the new badge duplicate the version on the menu/settings. *Accepted* per Q3a (badge is reinforced, not consolidated); noted as intentional.
- **Assumption —** `VERSION_LABEL_TEXT` is always available in scenes (it already is, via build-time `define`).
- **Assumption —** the Game Selector title has enough headroom above `y = 30` to stack a badge; if not, the badge may overlap the title's top edge (permitted by option (c)).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Temptation to restyle other HUD chrome or remove the muted version labels. Record such opportunities as linked work items, do not expand scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Context gathered before asking: all menu/game/Gym titles route through `createSceneTitle()`/`createSceneHeader()` (`src/ui/SceneHeader.ts`), the menu title is a one-off in `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`, the settings title is in `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, and `HelpPanel.ts` has no title heading. The version string already exists as build-time `__APP_VERSION__` (`src/ui/versionDisplay.ts`, currently `v0.1.17`).

- **Q1 — Visual form and placement of the ALPHA banner?**
  Options: (a) inline red pill badge to the right of each title; (b) full-width red ribbon at the canvas top; (c) red badge stacked above/over the title. Agent recommendation: (a) — keeps the title as the anchor and avoids covering HUD buttons.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (c)** — red badge stacked above/over the title.

- **Q2 — Which surfaces receive the banner?**
  Options: (a) every title (GameSelector, all example games, all Gym scenes, Help + Settings); (b) game and menu titles only; (c) menu + Help/Settings only. Agent recommendation: (a) — item says "all game screens".
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — every title, including Help and Settings headers.

- **Q3 — Help/Settings pane treatment and existing version labels?**
  Options: (a) badge on SettingsPanel title + compact "Help" + ALPHA header on HelpPanel, keep existing muted version labels; (b) SettingsPanel only; (c) remove the existing muted version labels. Agent recommendation: (a) — covers both panes while preserving existing labels.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — SettingsPanel + compact HelpPanel header; keep existing muted version labels.

data.description:
## Goal

Make every event card's coin/reputation text equal its current integer `card-data.csv` value so the text states the amount the engine actually applies (AC1).

## Context

Producer decision (OPEN QUESTION 1, answer A): `text = data`. 43 events are a plain ×100 rescale; 19 events have pre-existing rebalance drift and must be set to the current data value; 9 percent/duration/no-effect events are unchanged. Data columns must not change (no rebalancing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every coin/reputation mention in all 71 event `effect` values equals the matching `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` (rule A). Examples: `evt-harvest-festival` → `+600 coins to each Food business and +450 reputation`; `evt-charity-drive` → `+1350 reputation`.
- `evt-shopping-spree` `description` fraction `+2.5 coins` → `+250 coins`; no fractional coin/reputation value remains anywhere in the CSV.
- Percentages (`45%`, `80%`, `120%`), durations (`3 turns`), hand-slot counts, levels and the `{SYNERGY_RATE}` token are unchanged.
- No `card-data.csv` data column value changes (text-only diff).
- The `card-text-data-consistency` regression test passes.
- `npm run build` succeeds.

**Key Files:**

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/golf/replay.test.ts Replay CLI -- transcript validation
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
AssertionError: expected Error: Could not auto-detect game type (fixture not found at ../../example-games/golf/tests/fixtures/transcripts/fixture-game.json) to contain version
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout `dev` (the failure is reproducible at `a341ec3c`).
2. Run the failing test with **no** `GAMES_CONFIG` override (the documented default unit profile):
   `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts`
   (equivalent: `/skill:test --type unit`)
3. Observe 4 failures in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (12 passed, 5 skipped):
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for wrong transcript version`
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for missing initialState`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should reject v1 transcript when --stop-at is used`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should accept v1 transcript for regular replay (no --stop-at)`
4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Root Cause & Reproduction

`scripts/replay.ts` is core-owned and registers replay adapters from the **active build preset** via `registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())`. The default preset is `core-only` (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` → `DEFAULT_PRESET`), which registers **no** adapters. Adapter auto-detection then fails with `Could not auto-detect game type from transcript. Available adapters: none.` (and `--game golf` fails with `Unknown game type 'golf'. Available adapters: none`).

`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }`, so it inherits whatever `GAMES_CONFIG` the runner provides:

- **Red:** a bare `npx vitest run --project unit …` and the project-local `/skill:test --type unit` profile (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) do **not** export `GAMES_CONFIG`, so the preset is `core-only` and the 4 tests above fail.
- **Green:** `npm test`, `npm run test:smoke` and `npm run test:dev` set `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` in their shell runners, so the golf adapter is registered and the tests pass.

A separate **latent** defect was already fixed on `dev` while this plan ran: `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` was `'../../example-games/golf/…'`, resolving one level above the repo root (introduced when the test moved to `tests/golf/` in `fbee2e51`). Corrected to `'example-games/golf/…'` in `a341ec3c`. That fix is necessary but **not sufficient** — under `core-only` the test still fails.

## Chosen Fix (producer-confirmed 2026-09-26)

**Option 1 — test-local, keep the test hermetic.** Export the preset the test needs to the spawned CLI, e.g. in `runReplay()`:

```ts
env: { ...process.env, GAMES_CONFIG: process.env.GAMES_CONFIG ?? 'full' },
```

Rationale: `/skill:test --type unit` is the documented "minimum bar for every change" and `npx vitest run --project unit tests/<game>/` is the documented targeted command, so this file must pass with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset. Forcing `full` only as a fallback preserves an explicitly supplied preset and keeps the core unit profiles runnable under `core-only` — consistent with `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` ("core test profiles must stay runnable even with a bad `GAMES_CONFIG`").

**Rejected (Option 2):** adding `GAMES_CONFIG=full` to the `unit`/`smoke`/`dev` commands in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`. This is agent infrastructure out of bounds for agents and would not fix a bare `npx vitest run` for a developer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` passes under the **default unit profile with no `GAMES_CONFIG` override** — `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (and `/skill:test --type unit`) reports 0 failures — while continuing to pass under `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (`npm test`).
2. The test documents (in a code comment) why it pins `GAMES_CONFIG` to the full preset, and the already-corrected `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path (`example-games/golf/…`) is preserved. Related documentation is updated if any workflow/profile behaviour changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

**Key Files:**

- `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` — set the `GAMES_CONFIG` fallback in the spawned CLI env; document the preset dependency; keep the corrected fixture path.
- `scripts/replay.ts` — context only: preset-driven adapter registration (`registerConfiguredAdapters`); no change expected.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — context only: `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'`; no change expected.

**Note:** the two `scripts/` paths are context only; the fix is confined to the test file.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-26 (plan skill): Auto-plan pre-check returned **skip** (Effort Extra Small / Risk Low). During the run another agent closed the item (`completed`, commit `a341ec3c`), which fixed only the latent fixture path. Re-verified `dev` at `a341ec3c`: still 4 failures under the default unit profile; an OPEN QUESTION was recorded and the item was flagged for producer review. Producer answered **reopen** + **Option 1**; item re-claimed `in_progress`, description updated with root cause, chosen fix, refined ACs, Key Files and this changelog. No children created (Extra Small item, auto-complete path); coverage review `proceed`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Questions asked during the plan run

- **Q: The item was closed mid-session but the test still fails under the default `unit` profile — should it be reopened, or should a follow-up be filed?** — **Answer (producer): reopen.** Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26. Evidence: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (GAMES_CONFIG unset) → 4 failed / 12 passed / 5 skipped on `dev` at `a341ec3c`; comment recorded on the work item.
- **Q: Which fix is intended — (1) test-local `GAMES_CONFIG` fallback in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts`, or (2) `GAMES_CONFIG=full` in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`?** — **Answer (producer): Option 1 (test-local).** Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26. Final: Option 1.

### Research summary

`wl show CG-0MUILDS3200656TU` and the parent `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` established the seed context. Reproduction on `dev` (`a341ec3c`) with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset produced 4 failures; the same file passes with `GAMES_CONFIG=full`. `scripts/replay.ts` → `registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())` and `scripts/adapters/index.ts` showed preset-driven, dynamic adapter registration, with `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'` in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`. `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }`. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` and `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` each `export GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"`, whereas `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`'s typed commands do not. `git show fbee2e51` confirmed the `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path regression on the move to `tests/golf/`; `git diff dev -- tests/golf/replay.test.ts` in worktree `wl-CG-0MUIH2ZZY0019MG2` confirmed the `a341ec3c` correction.

### Open questions

None remaining.

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Root Cause & Fix

- **Root cause:** the two tests in this file that spawn a nested Vitest CLI
  (`runFixtureWithTapReporter`, `spawnSync` budget 180s) relied on Vitest's
  default 15s per-test timeout. Under host contention the nested `npx vitest`
  boot takes ~14s (Vite + Vitest startup), crossing the limit: the test times
  out while the synchronous child keeps running, and the run also reports an
  unhandled `[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"` error (see Map's
  root-cause comment on this item).
- **Fix:** give both nested-CLI tests an explicit per-test timeout
  `FIXTURE_CLI_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` — below the 180s `spawnSync` cap, so a
  genuine hang is still bounded while a slow boot cannot fail the tests.
- **Fix location:** already applied in the `CG-0MUGSBM8S007ETU5` worktree and
  lands in the same commit as that work item.

## Plan

No child work items are required. The change is a single-file, Extra Small
test-stability fix already implemented alongside parent `CG-0MUGSBM8S007ETU5`.
This item advances to `plan_complete` and is verified/closed when that commit
lands on `dev` and the named test passes.
